title.zh: 卷一百四十八 列傳第三十六 楊士奇 楊榮 楊溥
title.en: Volume 148 Biographies 36: Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, Yang Pu
title.raw: 卷一百四十八 列傳第三十六 楊士奇 楊榮 楊溥 Volume 148 Biographies 36: Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, Yang Pu

sentences.zh: 楊士奇 楊榮曾:孫旦 楊溥附:馬愉

translations.literal: Yang Shiqi; Yang Rong—see: Sun Dan; Yang Pu—appendix: Ma Yu
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shiqi; Yang Rong (see the biography of Sun Dan); Yang Pu (with appended biography of Ma Yu)

sentences.zh: 楊士奇

translations.literal: Yang Shiqi
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shiqi

sentences.zh: 楊士奇，名寓，以字行，泰和人。

translations.literal: Yang Shiqi, personal name Yu, known by his style name, was a native of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shiqi, whose personal name was Yu but who was known by his style name Shiqi, came from Taihe.

sentences.zh: 早孤，隨母適羅氏，已而復宗。

translations.literal: He lost his father early; he followed his mother in marrying into the Luo family, and afterward returned to his original clan.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he went with his mother when she married into the Luo family, but later reverted to his birth clan.

sentences.zh: 貧甚。

translations.literal: He was extremely poor.
translations.idiomatic: The family was desperately poor.

sentences.zh: 力學，授徒自給。

translations.literal: He studied diligently and supported himself by teaching pupils.
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself to learning and earned a living as a schoolmaster.

sentences.zh: 多游湖、湘間，館江夏最久。

translations.literal: He traveled much between the lakes and Hunan region, and lodged longest at Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled widely through the lake districts and Hunan, spending the longest stretch as a tutor in Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 建文初，集諸儒修《太祖實錄》，士奇已用薦征授教授當行，王叔英復以史才薦。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign, scholars were assembled to compile the Veritable Records of the Taizu Emperor; Shiqi had already been summoned on recommendation to take up an appointment as professor and was about to depart, when Wang Shuying again recommended him for his talent as a historian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwen era, when scholars were gathered to compile the Veritable Records of Taizu, Shiqi had already been recommended and summoned to a professorship and was preparing to leave, but Wang Shuying recommended him again for his gifts as a historian.

sentences.zh: 遂召入翰林，充編纂官。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as a compiling official.
translations.idiomatic: He was then called to the Hanlin Academy to serve as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 尋命吏部考第史館諸儒。

translations.literal: Soon the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to rank the scholars of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Ministry of Personnel was instructed to rank the historians in the institute.

sentences.zh: 尚書張紞得士奇策，曰：「此非經生言也。」

translations.literal: Minister Zhang Yi obtained Shiqi's examination essay and said, "These are not the words of a mere classicist."
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Zhang Yi read Shiqi's examination paper, he remarked, "This is not the writing of a pedantic classicist."

sentences.zh: 奏第一。

translations.literal: He reported him ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked him first in his report.

sentences.zh: 授吳王府審理副，仍供館職。

translations.literal: He was appointed assistant judge of the Prince of Wu's establishment, while still performing his duties at the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi was made assistant judge on the staff of the Prince of Wu, while continuing his academy duties.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，改編修。

translations.literal: When Chengzu took the throne, he was changed to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengzu acceded, he was promoted to compiler.

sentences.zh: 已，簡入內閣，典機務。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was selected to enter the Grand Secretariat and direct state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon chosen for the Grand Secretariat, where he handled affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 數月進侍講。

translations.literal: Several months later he was advanced to attendant lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was promoted to attendant lecturer.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年選宮僚，以士奇為左中允。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle, palace staff were selected, and Shiqi was made left vice director of the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 2, when the heir apparent's staff was chosen, Shiqi was appointed left vice director of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五年進左諭德。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was advanced to left mentor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to left mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 士奇奉職甚謹，私居不言公事，雖至親厚不得聞。

translations.literal: Shiqi was extremely scrupulous in office; in private he did not speak of public business, so that even his closest intimates could not hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi served with exceptional discretion: at home he never discussed official business, so that even his nearest kin knew nothing of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 在帝前，舉止恭慎，善應對，言事輒中。

translations.literal: Before the emperor his bearing was respectful and cautious; he was skilled in replies, and whenever he spoke on affairs he hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: In the emperor's presence he was deferential and measured, answered well, and his counsel was invariably on target.

sentences.zh: 人有小過，嘗為揜覆之。

translations.literal: When others had minor faults, he would cover them up.
translations.idiomatic: He often shielded colleagues from blame for small mistakes.

sentences.zh: 廣東布政使徐奇載嶺南土物饋廷臣，或得其目籍以進。

translations.literal: Xu Qi, provincial administration commissioner of Guangdong, sent local products of Lingnan as gifts to court officials; someone obtained the list of recipients and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qi, the Guangdong provincial commissioner, sent gifts of Lingnan products to court officials, and someone obtained the list of names and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝閱無士奇名，召問。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and, finding no name of Shiqi, summoned and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noticed Shiqi's name was missing and summoned him to ask why.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「奇赴廣時，群臣作詩文贈行，臣適病弗預，以故獨不及。

translations.literal: He replied, "When Qi was leaving for Guang, the ministers composed poems and essays to send him off; I happened to be ill and did not take part, and for that reason alone I was not included.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "When Xu Qi left for Guangdong, the ministers wrote parting poems and essays; I was ill at the time and took no part, which is why my name alone is absent.

sentences.zh: 今受否未可知，且物微，當無他意。」

translations.literal: Whether he has now accepted or not cannot yet be known; moreover the goods are trifling, and there should be no other intention."
translations.idiomatic: Whether he has accepted anything since is unclear in any case, and the gifts are slight; there is surely no ulterior motive."

sentences.zh: 帝遽命毀籍。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered the list destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once ordered the list burned.

sentences.zh: 六年，帝北巡，命與蹇義、黃淮留輔太子。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the emperor toured the north and ordered him, together with Jian Yi and Huang Huai, to remain and assist the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when the emperor toured the north, he left Shiqi with Jian Yi and Huang Huai to assist the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子喜文辭，贊善王汝玉以詩法進。

translations.literal: The crown prince delighted in literary composition; the tutor Wang Ruyu advanced by teaching poetic craft.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince loved belles lettres, and his tutor Wang Ruyu won favor by teaching him poetry.

sentences.zh: 士奇曰：「殿下當留意《六經》，暇則觀兩漢詔令。

translations.literal: Shiqi said, "Your Highness should attend to the Six Classics; in leisure hours you may read the edicts and orders of the two Han dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said, "Your Highness ought to focus on the Six Classics, and in spare moments study the edicts of the Former and Later Han.

sentences.zh: 詩小技，不足為也。」

translations.literal: Poetry is a minor skill and not worth pursuing."
translations.idiomatic: Poetry is a minor accomplishment and not worth your effort."

sentences.zh: 太子稱善。

translations.literal: The crown prince praised this as right.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince agreed that this was sound advice.

sentences.zh: 初，帝起兵時，漢王數力戰有功。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor raised his army, the Prince of Han fought hard many times and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Chengzu first raised his army, the Prince of Han had fought bravely and won distinction.

sentences.zh: 帝許以事成立為太子。

translations.literal: The emperor had promised that when the enterprise succeeded he would be made crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had promised that if their cause succeeded, the Prince of Han would be made heir.

sentences.zh: 既而不得立，怨望。

translations.literal: Afterward he was not established as heir and nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When he was passed over, he grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 帝又憐趙王年少，寵異之。

translations.literal: The emperor also pitied the Prince of Zhao for his youth and favored him exceptionally.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also favored the young Prince of Zhao with special indulgence.

sentences.zh: 由是兩王合而間太子，帝頗心動。

translations.literal: Hence the two princes joined to sow discord against the crown prince, and the emperor's mind was somewhat moved.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes therefore worked together to undermine the heir, and the emperor began to waver.

sentences.zh: 九年還南京，召士奇問監國狀。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, returning to Nanjing, he summoned Shiqi and asked about conditions under the regency.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, on returning to Nanjing, he summoned Shiqi and asked how the crown prince had governed in his absence.

sentences.zh: 士奇以孝敬對，且曰：「殿下天資高，即有過必知，知必改，存心愛人，決不負陛下托。」

translations.literal: Shiqi answered with filial piety and respect, and added, "Your Highness's natural endowment is high: if he has faults he is sure to know them, and knowing them he is sure to correct them; his heart cherishes others, and he will certainly not fail the trust Your Majesty has placed in him."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi spoke of the heir's filial devotion and added, "Your Highness is gifted by nature: any fault he commits he recognizes, and once he recognizes it he corrects it. His heart is set on caring for others; he will never betray the charge Your Majesty has given him."

sentences.zh: 帝悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was reassured.

sentences.zh: 十一年正旦，日食。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the eleventh year there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the eleventh year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書呂震請勿罷朝賀。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Lü Zhen requested that the court congratulatory audience not be canceled.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Lü Zhen urged that the New Year court audience not be canceled.

sentences.zh: 侍郎儀智持不可。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Yi Zhi held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Yi Zhi objected that this would not do.

sentences.zh: 士奇亦引宋仁宗事力言之。

translations.literal: Shiqi also cited the precedent of Song Renzong and argued forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi also cited Emperor Renzong of Song and argued strenuously against holding the audience.

sentences.zh: 遂罷賀。

translations.literal: Thereupon the congratulatory audience was canceled.
translations.idiomatic: The celebration was canceled.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝北征。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor campaigned in the north.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor marched north on campaign.

sentences.zh: 士奇仍輔太子居守。

translations.literal: Shiqi again assisted the crown prince in residence and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi again remained to assist the crown prince in the capital.

sentences.zh: 漢王譖太子益急。

translations.literal: The Prince of Han slandered the crown prince with increasing urgency.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Han's accusations against the heir grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 帝還，以迎駕緩，盡征東宮官黃淮等下獄。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, because the welcome had been slow, he summoned all the eastern-palace officials including Huang Huai and imprisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, he imprisoned the entire eastern-palace staff, including Huang Huai, on the charge that the welcome had been tardy.

sentences.zh: 士奇後至，宥之。

translations.literal: Shiqi arrived later and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi arrived later and was spared.

sentences.zh: 召問太子事。

translations.literal: He was summoned and questioned about the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him and questioned him about the heir.

sentences.zh: 士奇頓首言：「太子孝敬如初。

translations.literal: Shiqi kowtowed and said, "The crown prince's filial respect is as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi kowtowed and said, "The crown prince's filial devotion is unchanged.

sentences.zh: 凡所稽遲，皆臣等罪。」

translations.literal: All delay was the fault of your servants."
translations.idiomatic: Any delay in the welcome was entirely our fault."

sentences.zh: 帝意解。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was eased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 行在諸臣交章劾士奇不當獨宥，遂下錦衣衛獄，尋釋之。

translations.literal: The officials at the traveling palace submitted memorials one after another impeaching Shiqi for being improperly pardoned alone; he was then sent down to the Embroidered-Uniform Guard prison, and soon released.
translations.idiomatic: Officials with the imperial entourage memorialized in succession that Shiqi ought not to have been pardoned alone; he was sent to the Embroidered-Uniform Guard prison but released shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 十四年，帝還京師，微聞漢王奪嫡謀及諸不軌狀，以問蹇義。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the emperor returned to the capital, having faintly heard of the Prince of Han's plot to seize the succession and various other irregular acts, and questioned Jian Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, after returning to the capital, the emperor had heard vague reports of the Prince of Han's designs on the succession and other disloyal conduct, and he questioned Jian Yi.

sentences.zh: 義不對，乃問士奇。

translations.literal: Yi did not answer, and he then questioned Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi would not speak, so the emperor turned to Shiqi.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣與義俱侍東宮，外人無敢為臣兩人言漢王事者。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant and Yi both attend the eastern palace; outsiders do not dare speak to us two of the Prince of Han's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Jian Yi and I both serve the eastern palace; no outsider dares discuss the Prince of Han with either of us.

sentences.zh: 然漢王兩遣就籓，皆不肯行。

translations.literal: Yet the Prince of Han was twice sent to his fief and both times refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor twice ordered the Prince of Han to take up his fief, and both times he refused.

sentences.zh: 今知陛下將徙都，輒請留守南京。

translations.literal: Now learning that Your Majesty will move the capital, he promptly requests to remain and guard Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he knows Your Majesty plans to move the capital, he has asked to remain and guard Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下熟察其意。」

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty carefully examine his intention."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty alone can judge what he intends by this."

sentences.zh: 帝默然，起還宮。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent, rose, and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing, rose, and withdrew to the palace.

sentences.zh: 居數日，帝盡得漢王事，削兩護衛，處之樂安。

translations.literal: After several days the emperor had fully learned the Prince of Han's affairs, stripped him of two guard units, and settled him at Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the emperor had uncovered the full story, stripped the prince of two guard regiments, and transferred him to Le'an.

sentences.zh: 明年進士奇翰林學士，兼故官。

translations.literal: The next year Shiqi was advanced to Hanlin academician, while retaining his former office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shiqi was promoted to Hanlin academician while keeping his previous post.

sentences.zh: 十九年改左春坊大學士，仍兼學士。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was changed to grand secretary of the left Eastern Palace, still concurrently holding academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was made grand secretary of the left Eastern Palace, retaining his academician title.

sentences.zh: 明年復坐輔導有闕，下錦衣衛獄，旬日而釋。

translations.literal: The next year he again sat in guilt for faults in tutoring, was sent down to the Embroidered-Uniform Guard prison, and released after ten days.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was again imprisoned in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard prison for failures in tutoring the heir, and released after ten days.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，擢禮部侍郎兼華蓋殿大學士。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, he was promoted to vice minister of rites and concurrently grand secretary of the Huagai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong acceded, Shiqi was promoted to vice minister of rites and grand secretary of the Huagai Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝御便殿，蹇義、夏原吉奏事未退。

translations.literal: The emperor was at the informal hall; Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji were reporting affairs and had not yet withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor was in the informal audience hall while Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji were still reporting on affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝望見士奇，謂二人曰：「新華蓋學士來，必有讜言，試共聽之。」

translations.literal: The emperor saw Shiqi in the distance and said to the two, "The new Huagai academician has come; he is sure to have forthright words—let us try listening together."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Shiqi approach, the emperor said to them, "The new Huagai grand secretary is here; he is bound to have honest counsel. Let us hear him together."

sentences.zh: 士奇入言：「恩詔減歲供甫下二日，惜薪司傳旨征棗八十萬斤，與前詔戾。」

translations.literal: Shiqi entered and said, "The grace edict reducing the annual tribute had been issued only two days before, yet the Department for Economizing Fuel transmitted an order to levy eight hundred thousand jin of jujubes, which contradicts the prior edict."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi came in and said, "The grace edict reducing annual levies was issued only two days ago, yet the Department for Economizing Fuel has ordered eight hundred thousand jin of jujubes collected—this contradicts the earlier decree."

sentences.zh: 帝立命減其半。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered the levy halved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately ordered the levy cut in half.

sentences.zh: 服制二十七日期滿，呂震請即吉。

translations.literal: When the twenty-seven-day mourning period ended, Lü Zhen requested immediate resumption of auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: When the twenty-seven-day mourning period ended, Lü Zhen urged the emperor to resume normal dress at once.

sentences.zh: 士奇不可。

translations.literal: Shiqi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi objected.

sentences.zh: 震厲聲叱之。

translations.literal: Zhen rebuked him in a harsh voice.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen shouted him down.

sentences.zh: 蹇義兼取二說進。

translations.literal: Jian Yi took both views together and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi presented both sides to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝素冠麻衣絰而視朝。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor attended court in a plain cap, hemp garments, and mourning sash.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor held court wearing plain mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 廷臣惟士奇及英國公張輔服如之。

translations.literal: Among the court officials only Shiqi and the Duke of Ying, Zhang Fu, were dressed likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Of the entire court, only Shiqi and the Duke of Ying, Zhang Fu, dressed in mourning as well.

sentences.zh: 朝罷，帝謂左右曰：「梓宮在殯，易服豈臣子所忍言，士奇執是也。」

translations.literal: After court the emperor said to those beside him, "The imperial coffin is still in mourning hall—how could a subject bear to speak of changing dress? Shiqi was right to hold firm."
translations.idiomatic: After court the emperor told his attendants, "With the late emperor's coffin still in the hall, how could any loyal subject propose changing dress? Shiqi was right to insist."

sentences.zh: 進少保，與同官楊榮、金幼孜並賜「繩愆糾繆」銀章，得密封言事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to junior guardian; together with his colleagues Yang Rong and Jin Youzi he was granted silver seals reading "Correct faults and rectify errors," and permitted to memorialize in sealed reports.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to junior guardian; he and his colleagues Yang Rong and Jin Youzi were given silver seals inscribed "Correct faults and rectify errors," with the privilege of submitting sealed memorials.

sentences.zh: 尋進少傅。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 時籓司守令來朝，尚書李慶建議發軍伍余馬給有司，歲課其駒。

translations.literal: At that time provincial and prefectural officials came to court; Minister Li Qing proposed distributing surplus army horses to local offices and levying their foals annually.
translations.idiomatic: When provincial and prefectural officials came to court, Minister Li Qing proposed assigning surplus army horses to local governments and taxing them annually for foals.

sentences.zh: 士奇曰：「朝廷選賢授官，乃使牧馬，是貴畜而賤士也，何以示天下後世。」

translations.literal: Shiqi said, "The court selects the worthy and appoints them to office, yet would have them herd horses—this values beasts and despises scholars; how can this be shown to the realm and to posterity?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said, "The court selects men of talent for office only to set them herding horses—this honors livestock and debases scholars. What lesson would that teach the empire and posterity?"

sentences.zh: 帝許中旨罷之，已而寂然。

translations.literal: The emperor assented in an oral edict to abolish it, but afterward all was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor orally agreed to cancel the plan, but nothing more was heard.

sentences.zh: 士奇復力言。

translations.literal: Shiqi again argued forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi pressed the matter again.

sentences.zh: 又不報。

translations.literal: Again there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Again he received no reply.

sentences.zh: 有頃，帝御思善門，召士奇謂曰：「朕向者豈真忘之。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor was at the Sishan Gate, summoned Shiqi, and said, "Did I truly forget it before?
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, at the Sishan Gate, the emperor summoned Shiqi and said, "Did you think I had truly forgotten?

sentences.zh: 聞呂震、李慶輩皆不喜卿，朕念卿孤立，恐為所傷，不欲因卿言罷耳，今有辭矣。」

translations.literal: I heard that Lü Zhen, Li Qing, and their sort all dislike you; I thought of you standing alone and feared you might be harmed, and did not wish to abolish it on your word alone—now there is a pretext."
translations.idiomatic: I heard that Lü Zhen, Li Qing, and their faction dislike you. I knew you stood alone and feared they would harm you, so I did not want to cancel the plan solely on your advice. Now I have grounds to act."

sentences.zh: 手出陝西按察使陳智言養馬不便疏，使草敕行之。

translations.literal: He handed him a memorial from Shaanxi surveillance commissioner Chen Zhi stating the inconvenience of raising horses, and ordered him to draft an edict to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: He handed him a memorial from Shaanxi surveillance commissioner Chen Zhi on the burdens of horse-rearing and told him to draft an edict abolishing the policy.

sentences.zh: 士奇頓首謝。

translations.literal: Shiqi kowtowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 群臣習朝正旦儀，呂震請用樂，士奇與黃淮疏止。

translations.literal: The ministers were accustomed to the New Year's Day court ritual; Lü Zhen requested the use of music, and Shiqi with Huang Huai submitted a memorial to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers were rehearsing the New Year's court ceremony when Lü Zhen proposed using music; Shiqi and Huang Huai memorialized against it.

sentences.zh: 未報。

translations.literal: There was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: No reply came.

sentences.zh: 士奇復奏，待庭中至夜漏十刻。

translations.literal: Shiqi memorialized again and waited in the courtyard until the night watch of the tenth double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi memorialized again and waited in the courtyard until the tenth watch of the night.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Approval finally came.

sentences.zh: 越日，帝召謂曰：「震每事誤朕，非卿等言，悔無及。」

translations.literal: The next day the emperor summoned him and said, "Zhen errs in every matter and misleads Us; had it not been for your words, regret would have been beyond remedy."
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor told him, "Lü Zhen misleads me on every issue; without your counsel, I would have had no way to undo the damage."

sentences.zh: 命兼兵部尚書，並食三祿。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve concurrently as minister of war and to draw three stipends.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed concurrent minister of war with three stipends.

sentences.zh: 士奇辭尚書祿。

translations.literal: Shiqi declined the minister's stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi declined the ministerial stipend.

sentences.zh: 帝監國時，憾御史舒仲成，至是欲罪之。

translations.literal: While the emperor had been regent, he had resented Censor Shu Zhongcheng; now he wished to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor had been regent, he had resented Censor Shu Zhongcheng; now he wished to punish him.

sentences.zh: 士奇曰：「陛下即位，詔向忤旨者皆得宥。

translations.literal: Shiqi said: "When Your Majesty took the throne, you issued an edict pardoning all who had previously offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said, "When Your Majesty took the throne, you issued an edict pardoning all who had previously offended the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 若治仲成，則詔書不信，懼者眾矣。

translations.literal: If Zhongcheng is punished, the edict will no longer be trusted and many will grow fearful.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhongcheng is punished, the edict will no longer be trusted and many will grow fearful.

sentences.zh: 如漢景帝之待衛綰，不亦可乎？」

translations.literal: Would it not do, as when Emperor Jing of Han treated Wei Wan?"
translations.idiomatic: Would it not do, as when Emperor Jing of Han treated Wei Wan?"

sentences.zh: 帝即罷弗治。

translations.literal: The emperor at once dropped the case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once dropped the case.

sentences.zh: 或有言大理卿虞謙言事不密。

translations.literal: Someone said that Minister of Justice Yu Qian had spoken on affairs without discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said that Minister of Justice Yu Qian had spoken on affairs without discretion.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，降一官。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted him one rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and demoted him one rank.

sentences.zh: 士奇為白其罔，得復秩。

translations.literal: Shiqi cleared him of falsehood, and he recovered his rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi cleared him of falsehood, and he recovered his rank.

sentences.zh: 又大理少卿弋謙以言事得罪。

translations.literal: Then Vice Minister of Justice Yi Qian offended the throne by speaking on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Then Vice Minister of Justice Yi Qian offended the throne by speaking on affairs.

sentences.zh: 士奇曰：「謙應詔陳言。

translations.literal: Shiqi said: "Qian was responding to the edict by speaking forthrightly.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said, "Qian was responding to the edict by speaking forthrightly.

sentences.zh: 若加之罪，則群臣自此結舌矣。」

translations.literal: If he is punished, the ministers from this day forward will fall silent."
translations.idiomatic: If he is punished, the ministers from this day forward will fall silent."

sentences.zh: 帝立進謙副都御史，而下敕引過。

translations.literal: The emperor at once promoted Qian to Vice Censor-in-Chief and issued an edict acknowledging his own fault.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once promoted Qian to Vice Censor-in-Chief and issued an edict acknowledging his own fault.

sentences.zh: 時有上書頌太平者，帝以示諸大臣，皆以為然。

translations.literal: At that time someone submitted a memorial praising the age as peaceful; the emperor showed it to the ministers, and all thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: Someone then submitted a memorial praising the reign as an age of peace; the emperor showed it to the ministers, and all agreed.

sentences.zh: 士奇獨曰：「陛下雖澤被天下，然流徙尚未歸，瘡痍尚未復，民尚艱食。

translations.literal: Shiqi alone said, "Although Your Majesty's grace covers the realm, the displaced have not yet returned, the wounds are not yet healed, and the people still lack sufficient food.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi alone said, "Although Your Majesty's grace reaches every corner of the realm, refugees have not yet returned home, the land has not yet recovered from war, and the people still lack enough to eat.

sentences.zh: 更休息數年，庶幾太平可期。」

translations.literal: After several more years of rest, perhaps peace may be expected."
translations.idiomatic: Give the realm a few more years to recover, and true peace may then be within reach."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 因顧蹇義等曰：「朕待御等以至誠，望匡弼。

translations.literal: He then turned to Jian Yi and the others and said, "We treat you with utmost sincerity and hope you will correct and assist Us.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Jian Yi and the others, he added, "I treat you with complete sincerity and look to you for honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 惟士奇曾五上章，卿等皆無一言。

translations.literal: Only Shiqi has submitted five memorials, while you all have not spoken a word.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi alone has memorialized five times, yet none of you has said a word.

sentences.zh: 豈果朝無闕政，天下太平耶？」

translations.literal: Can it truly be that the court has no flawed policies and the realm is at peace?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you truly believe the court has no faults and the realm is already at peace?"

sentences.zh: 諸臣慚謝。

translations.literal: The ministers apologized in shame.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers withdrew in shame to apologize.

sentences.zh: 是年四月，帝賜士奇璽書曰：「往者朕膺監國之命，卿侍左右，同心合德，徇國忘身，屢歷艱虞，曾不易志。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year the emperor bestowed on Shiqi an imperial letter saying, "Formerly when We received the charge of regency, you attended at Our side, of one heart and virtue, devoted to the state and forgetful of self, repeatedly passing through hardship and peril, never changing your purpose.
translations.idiomatic: That April the emperor sent Shiqi an imperial letter: "When I bore the charge of regency, you stood at my side in loyal unity, giving yourself to the state and forgetting your own safety. You endured repeated trials without wavering in purpose.

sentences.zh: 及朕嗣位以來，嘉謨入告，期予於治，正固不二，簡在朕心。

translations.literal: Since We succeeded to the throne, excellent counsel has been presented, expecting Us toward good government; upright and unwavering, you are chosen in Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: Since my accession your wise counsel has guided me toward good government. Your steadfast integrity has earned my deepest trust.

sentences.zh: 茲創製『楊貞，一印賜卿，尚克交修，以成明良之譽。」

translations.literal: Now We have newly made the seal 'Yang Zhenjie' and bestow it on you; may you still be able to mutually cultivate virtue and achieve the praise of a wise ruler and good minister."
translations.idiomatic: I have had a seal inscribed 'Yang Zhenjie' made for you. May we continue to refine each other's virtue and earn the renown of a wise ruler and loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 尋修《太宗實錄》，與黃淮、金幼孜、楊溥俱充總裁官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he compiled the Veritable Records of Taizong, and together with Huang Huai, Jin Youzi, and Yang Pu all served as chief compilers.
translations.idiomatic: He soon helped compile the Veritable Records of Taizong, serving as chief compiler alongside Huang Huai, Jin Youzi, and Yang Pu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝不豫，召士奇與蹇義、黃淮、楊榮至思善門，命士奇書敕召太子於南京。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor fell ill and summoned Shiqi with Jian Yi, Huang Huai, and Yang Rong to the Sishan Gate, ordering Shiqi to draft an edict summoning the crown prince from Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor fell ill. He summoned Shiqi, Jian Yi, Huang Huai, and Yang Rong to the Sishan Gate and ordered Shiqi to draft an edict calling the crown prince from Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，修《仁宗實錄》，仍充總裁。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, he compiled the Veritable Records of Renzong and again served as chief compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong acceded, Shiqi again served as chief compiler of the Veritable Records of Renzong.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年，漢王高煦反。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande, the Prince of Han, Gao Xu, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 1, the Prince of Han, Zhu Gaoxu, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 帝親征，平之。

translations.literal: The emperor campaigned in person and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led the campaign in person and crushed the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 師還，次獻縣之單家橋，侍郎陳山迎謁，言漢、趙二王實同心，請乘勢襲彰德執趙王。

translations.literal: The army returned and halted at Danjia Bridge in Xian County; Vice Minister Chen Shan came to meet and reported that the Princes of Han and Zhao were truly of one mind, and requested taking advantage of the momentum to strike Zhangde and seize the Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march the army halted at Danjia Bridge in Xian County. Vice Minister Chen Shan came to meet the emperor and urged that the Princes of Han and Zhao had acted in concert, proposing a surprise attack on Zhangde to seize the Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 榮力贊決。

translations.literal: Rong strongly urged approval.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong strongly supported the plan.

sentences.zh: 士奇曰：「事當有實，天地鬼神可欺乎？」

translations.literal: Shiqi said, "Matters must have substance; can Heaven and Earth and the spirits be deceived?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said, "Charges must be grounded in fact. Can we deceive Heaven, Earth, and the spirits?"

sentences.zh: 榮厲聲曰：「汝欲撓大計耶！

translations.literal: Rong said in a harsh voice, "Do you wish to thwart the great plan?
translations.idiomatic: Rong snapped, "Are you trying to sabotage the grand strategy?

sentences.zh: 今逆黨言趙實與謀，何謂無辭？」

translations.literal: The rebels now say Zhao truly plotted with them—how can you say there is no pretext?"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels themselves say the Prince of Zhao was in on the plot. What more pretext do we need?"

sentences.zh: 士奇曰：「太宗皇帝三子，今上惟兩叔父。

translations.literal: Shiqi said, "Taizong the emperor had three sons; the present sovereign has only two uncles.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi replied, "Taizu had three sons; Your Majesty has only two surviving uncles.

sentences.zh: 有罪者不可赦，其無罪者宜厚待之，疑則防之，使無虞而已。

translations.literal: Those guilty cannot be pardoned; those without guilt should be generously treated—if there is doubt, guard against them so they give no cause for alarm, and that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The guilty cannot be pardoned, but the innocent should be treated generously. If you have doubts, guard against them—but that is all that is needed.

sentences.zh: 何遽加兵，傷皇祖在天意乎？」

translations.literal: Why hastily send troops and wound the intention of the imperial ancestor in Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Why rush to arms and offend your grandfather's spirit in Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 時惟楊溥與士奇合。

translations.literal: At that time only Yang Pu agreed with Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yang Pu sided with Shiqi.

sentences.zh: 將入諫，榮先入，士奇繼之，閽者不納。

translations.literal: About to enter and remonstrate, Rong entered first and Shiqi followed, but the gatekeepers would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: They were about to enter and remonstrate. Rong went in first, Shiqi followed, but the gatekeepers refused them entry.

sentences.zh: 尋召義、原吉入。

translations.literal: Soon Yi and Yuanji were summoned in.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji were soon summoned instead.

sentences.zh: 二人以士奇言白帝。

translations.literal: The two reported Shiqi's words to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They relayed Shiqi's argument to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝初無罪趙意，移兵事得寢。

translations.literal: The emperor had had no intention of condemning Zhao from the first, and the matter of moving troops was allowed to rest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had never intended to punish the Prince of Zhao, and the plan to move troops was dropped.

sentences.zh: 比還京，帝思士奇言，謂曰：「今議者多言趙王事，奈何？」

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital, the emperor thought of Shiqi's words and said to him, "Now the discussants mostly speak of the Prince of Zhao—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital, the emperor recalled Shiqi's counsel and asked him, "Many at court are still pressing the case against the Prince of Zhao. What should I do?"

sentences.zh: 士奇曰：「趙最親，陛下當保全之，毋惑群言。」

translations.literal: Shiqi said, "Zhao is the closest kin; Your Majesty should preserve him and not be misled by the multitude of words."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said, "The Prince of Zhao is your closest kinsman. Your Majesty should protect him and not be swayed by popular clamor."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾欲封群臣章示王，令自處何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I wish to seal up the ministers' memorials and show them to the prince, letting him handle matters himself—how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What if I seal up the ministers' memorials and send them to the prince, letting him judge his own case?"

sentences.zh: 士奇曰：「善，更得一璽書幸甚。」

translations.literal: Shiqi said, "Excellent; it would be even better to add an imperial letter."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said, "An excellent plan—and it would be even better to add a personal letter from Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 於是發使奉書至趙。

translations.literal: Thereupon envoys were dispatched bearing the letter to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent with the letter to the Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 趙王得書大喜。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhao, receiving the letter, was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was overjoyed when he received it.

sentences.zh: 泣曰：「吾生矣。」

translations.literal: Weeping, he said, "I shall live."
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, he said, "I am saved."

sentences.zh: 即上表謝，且獻護衛，言者始息。

translations.literal: He immediately submitted a memorial of thanks and also offered up his guard units; the talkers then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately submitted a memorial of thanks and offered to surrender his guard regiments, and the accusations finally died away.

sentences.zh: 帝待趙王日益親而薄陳山。

translations.literal: The emperor treated the Prince of Zhao with increasing intimacy and regarded Chen Shan coldly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew closer to the Prince of Zhao and colder toward Chen Shan.

sentences.zh: 謂士奇曰：「趙王所以全，卿力也。」

translations.literal: He said to Shiqi, "That the Prince of Zhao was preserved is your effort."
translations.idiomatic: He told Shiqi, "The prince owes his safety to you."

sentences.zh: 賜金幣。

translations.literal: He bestowed gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 時交阯數叛。

translations.literal: At that time Jiaozhi rebelled repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi rebelled repeatedly at this time.

sentences.zh: 屢發大軍征討，皆敗沒。

translations.literal: Large armies were repeatedly sent to campaign, and all were defeated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated large expeditions ended in defeat and ruin.

sentences.zh: 交阯黎利遣人偽請立陳氏後。

translations.literal: Li Li of Jiaozhi sent men falsely requesting the establishment of a descendant of the Chen house.
translations.idiomatic: Li Li of Jiaozhi sent envoys falsely proposing to restore a descendant of the Chen dynasty.

sentences.zh: 帝亦厭兵，欲許之。

translations.literal: The emperor also wearied of warfare and wished to agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor too had grown weary of war and was inclined to agree.

sentences.zh: 英國公張輔、尚書蹇義以下，皆言與之無名，徒示弱天下。

translations.literal: The Duke of Ying Zhang Fu, Minister Jian Yi, and those below all said that agreeing would be without justification and would merely show weakness to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Ying Zhang Fu, Minister Jian Yi, and others all argued that withdrawal would be unjustified and would only show weakness to the world.

sentences.zh: 帝召士奇、榮謀。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Shiqi and Rong to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Shiqi and Yang Rong for counsel.

sentences.zh: 二人力言：「陛下恤民命以綏荒服，不為無名。

translations.literal: The two argued forcefully, "Your Majesty cherishes the people's lives to pacify distant regions—this is not without justification.
translations.idiomatic: Both argued strenuously: "Your Majesty would spare the people's lives to pacify a distant province—that is justification enough.

sentences.zh: 漢棄珠厓，前史以為美談，不為示弱，許之便。」

translations.literal: When Han abandoned Zhuya, former histories took it as fine praise; it is not showing weakness—agreeing would be expedient."
translations.idiomatic: When the Han abandoned Hainan, historians praised it as wisdom. This is not weakness—agreement is the prudent course."

sentences.zh: 尋命擇使交阯者。

translations.literal: Soon he ordered the selection of an envoy to Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: He soon ordered an envoy chosen for Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 蹇義薦伏伯安口辨。

translations.literal: Jian Yi recommended Fu Bo'an for his eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi recommended Fu Bo'an for his gift of speech.

sentences.zh: 士奇曰：「言不忠信，雖蠻貊之邦不可行。

translations.literal: Shiqi said, "If words lack loyalty and trustworthiness, even among barbarian lands one may not go.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said, "Without loyalty and trustworthiness, an envoy cannot go even to barbarian lands.

sentences.zh: 伯安小人，往且辱國。」

translations.literal: Bo'an is a petty man; if sent he will disgrace the state."
translations.idiomatic: Bo'an is a scoundrel who would only bring shame on the empire."

sentences.zh: 帝是之，別遣使。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and dispatched another envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and chose someone else.

sentences.zh: 於是棄交阯，罷兵，歲省軍興巨萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jiaozhi was abandoned, troops were demobilized, and each year military expenses of tens of thousands were saved.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi was abandoned, the armies withdrawn, and millions in military expenditure saved each year.

sentences.zh: 五年春，帝奉皇太后謁陵，召英國公張輔、尚書蹇義及士奇、榮、幼孜、溥，朝太后於行殿。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year the emperor, attending the empress dowager in visiting the tombs, summoned the Duke of Ying Zhang Fu, Minister Jian Yi, and Shiqi, Rong, Youzi, and Pu to attend the empress dowager at the traveling hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year, while accompanying the empress dowager to the imperial tombs, the emperor summoned the Duke of Ying Zhang Fu, Minister Jian Yi, Shiqi, Yang Rong, Jin Youzi, and Yang Pu to pay court to the empress dowager at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 太后慰勞之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager comforted and encouraged them.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager received them with warm praise.

sentences.zh: 帝又語士奇曰：「太后為朕言，先帝在青宮，惟卿不憚觸忤，先帝能從，以不敗事。

translations.literal: The emperor also said to Shiqi, "The empress dowager told Us that when the late emperor was in the eastern palace, you alone did not fear giving offense; the late emperor could follow your counsel, and thus affairs did not fail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also told Shiqi, "The empress dowager said that when my father was crown prince, you alone dared speak unwelcome truth. He listened to you, and nothing went wrong.

sentences.zh: 又誨朕當受直言。」

translations.literal: She also admonished Us to accept forthright speech."
translations.idiomatic: She also urged me to welcome honest counsel."

sentences.zh: 士奇對曰：「此皇太后盛德之言，願陛下念之。」

translations.literal: Shiqi replied, "These are words of the empress dowager's great virtue; may Your Majesty keep them in mind."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi replied, "These are words of great wisdom from the empress dowager. I hope Your Majesty will take them to heart."

sentences.zh: 尋敕鴻臚寺。

translations.literal: Soon an order was issued to the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He soon issued an edict to the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 士奇老有疾，趨朝或後，毋論奏。

translations.literal: Shiqi was old and ill; if he came late to court, he was not to be impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shiqi was elderly and ill, he was not to be impeached if he arrived late at court.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗微行，夜幸士奇宅。

translations.literal: The emperor once traveled incognito and at night visited Shiqi's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor went out incognito and visited Shiqi's home at night.

sentences.zh: 士奇倉皇出迎，頓首曰：「陛下奈何以社稷宗廟之身自輕？」

translations.literal: Shiqi hurried out to receive him, kowtowed, and said, "Your Majesty—how can you lightly risk the body that bears the altars of state and the ancestral temple?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi rushed out to greet him and kowtowed. "Your Majesty, how can you risk the person who embodies the state and the ancestral temple?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕欲與卿一言，故來耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "We wished to speak a word with you—that is why We came."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I simply wanted a word with you—that is why I came."

sentences.zh: 後數日，獲二盜，有異謀。

translations.literal: Several days later two robbers were captured who had had unusual designs.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later two thieves with subversive plans were captured.

sentences.zh: 帝召士奇，告之故。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Shiqi and told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Shiqi and told him the story.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「今而後知卿之愛朕也。」

translations.literal: He added, "From now on We know your love for Us."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Now I understand how much you care for my safety."

sentences.zh: 帝以四方屢水旱，召士奇議下詔寬恤，免災傷租稅及官馬虧額者。

translations.literal: Because the four quarters repeatedly suffered flood and drought, the emperor summoned Shiqi to discuss issuing an edict of leniency and relief, remitting disaster-struck rents and taxes and shortfalls in official horses.
translations.idiomatic: With floods and droughts recurring across the realm, the emperor summoned Shiqi to discuss an edict of relief, remitting disaster-area taxes and penalties for shortfalls in official horse quotas.

sentences.zh: 士奇因請並蠲逋賦薪芻錢，減官田額，理冤滯，汰工役，以廣德意。

translations.literal: Shiqi thereupon requested also canceling overdue levies for fuel and fodder, reducing official-field quotas, clearing backlogged wrongs, and eliminating corvée labor, to extend the emperor's virtuous intent.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi also urged canceling overdue fuel and fodder levies, reducing official-field quotas, clearing backlogged cases, and cutting corvée burdens to extend the emperor's benevolence.

sentences.zh: 民大悅。

translations.literal: The people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 逾二年，帝謂士奇曰：「恤民詔下已久，今更有可恤者乎？」

translations.literal: After more than two years the emperor said to Shiqi, "The edict cherishing the people was issued long ago—is there anything more that can be relieved now?"
translations.idiomatic: More than two years later the emperor asked Shiqi, "The relief edict has been in force for some time. Is there anything more we can do for the people?"

sentences.zh: 士奇曰：「前詔減官田租，戶部征如故。」

translations.literal: Shiqi said, "The earlier edict reduced rents on official fields, but the Ministry of Revenue levies as before."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said, "The earlier edict reduced rents on official fields, but the Ministry of Revenue still collects at the old rate."

sentences.zh: 帝怫然曰：「今首行之，廢格者論如法。」

translations.literal: The emperor said angrily, "Let it be carried out from this day; those who nullify or obstruct it shall be punished according to law."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said angrily, "Implement it at once. Anyone who blocks it will be punished by law."

sentences.zh: 士奇復請撫逃民，察墨吏，舉文學、武勇之士，令極刑家子孫皆得仕進。

translations.literal: Shiqi again requested soothing fleeing commoners, investigating corrupt officials, recommending men of literary learning and martial valor, and allowing descendants of families punished with extreme penalties all to enter office.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi also urged resettling refugees, investigating corrupt officials, recommending men of literary and martial talent, and allowing descendants of families punished with capital crimes to enter government service.

sentences.zh: 又請廷臣三品以上及二司官，各舉所知，備方面郡守選。

translations.literal: He also requested that court officials of the third rank and above and provincial commissioners each recommend those they knew to supply candidates for frontier prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that officials of the third rank and above and provincial commissioners each recommend men they knew for provincial and prefectural appointments.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝勵精圖治，士奇等同心輔佐，海內號為治平。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor strove energetically to govern well; Shiqi and the others assisted with one heart, and within the seas it was called an age of good order.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor devoted himself to good government, Shiqi and his colleagues worked in concert, and the realm was hailed as well governed.

sentences.zh: 帝乃仿古君臣豫游事，每歲首，賜百官旬休。

translations.literal: The emperor then modeled the ancient practice of ruler and ministers sharing leisurely excursions; at the year's beginning he granted the hundred officials ten days' rest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor revived the ancient custom of ruler and ministers sharing leisure, granting officials ten days' holiday at the New Year.

sentences.zh: 車駕亦時幸西苑萬歲山，諸學士皆從。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage also from time to time visited the Western Park and Longevity Hill, and all the academicians followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would visit the Western Park and Longevity Hill, accompanied by all the Hanlin academicians.

sentences.zh: 賦詩賡和，從容問民間疾苦。

translations.literal: They composed and responded in verse, and at ease inquired into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: They composed poetry together and calmly discussed the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 有所論奏，帝皆虛懷聽納。

translations.literal: Whatever was presented in discussion and memorial, the emperor all received with open mind and adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever they proposed, the emperor listened with an open mind and accepted.

sentences.zh: 帝之初即位也，內閣臣七人。

translations.literal: When the emperor first took the throne, there were seven Grand Secretariat ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first took the throne, there were seven Grand Secretariat ministers.

sentences.zh: 陳山、張瑛以東宮舊恩入，不稱，出為他官。

translations.literal: Chen Shan and Zhang Ying had entered through old favor from the Eastern Palace; they proved unsuitable and were transferred to other offices.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shan and Zhang Ying had entered through old favor from the Eastern Palace; they proved unsuitable and were transferred to other offices.

sentences.zh: 黃淮以疾致仕。

translations.literal: Huang Huai retired on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Huai retired on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 金幼孜卒。

translations.literal: Jin Youzi died.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Youzi died.

sentences.zh: 閣中惟士奇、榮、溥三人。

translations.literal: In the Grand Secretariat only Shiqi, Rong, and Pu remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the Grand Secretariat only Shiqi, Rong, and Pu remained.

sentences.zh: 榮疏闓果毅，遇事敢為。

translations.literal: Rong was open and resolute, daring to act when affairs arose.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was open and resolute, daring to act when affairs arose.

sentences.zh: 數從成祖北征，能知邊將賢否、厄塞險易遠近、敵情順逆。

translations.literal: Having often followed Chengzu on northern campaigns, he knew which frontier commanders were worthy, the difficulty or ease of passes, their distance, and whether enemy dispositions were favorable or adverse.
translations.idiomatic: Having often followed Chengzu on northern campaigns, he knew which frontier commanders were worthy, the difficulty or ease of passes, their distance, and whether enemy dispositions were favorable or adverse.

sentences.zh: 然頗通饋遺，邊將歲時致良馬。

translations.literal: Yet he was rather free in receiving gifts; frontier commanders sent him fine horses at the turn of the year.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was rather free in receiving gifts; frontier commanders sent him fine horses at the turn of the year.

sentences.zh: 帝頗知之，以問士奇。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of this and asked Shiqi about it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of this and asked Shiqi about it.

sentences.zh: 士奇力言：「榮曉暢邊務，臣等不及，不宜以小眚介意。」

translations.literal: Shiqi urged forcefully: "Rong is thoroughly versed in frontier affairs—none of us equals him—and Your Majesty ought not mind a small fault."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi urged forcefully, "Rong is thoroughly versed in frontier affairs—none of us equals him—and Your Majesty ought not mind a small fault."

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「榮嘗短卿及原吉，卿乃為之地耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said: "Rong once spoke ill of you and Yuanji—are you now making excuses for him?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said, "Rong once spoke ill of you and Yuanji—are you now making excuses for him?"

sentences.zh: 士奇曰：「願陛下以曲容臣者容榮。」

translations.literal: Shiqi said: "I hope Your Majesty will extend to Rong the same indulgence you show me."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said, "I hope Your Majesty will extend to Rong the same indulgence you show me."

sentences.zh: 帝意乃解。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was thus set at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind was thus set at ease.

sentences.zh: 其後，語稍稍聞，榮以此愧士奇，相得甚歡。

translations.literal: Later word of this gradually spread; Rong was ashamed before Shiqi on this account, and the two became very close.
translations.idiomatic: Later word of this gradually spread; Rong was ashamed before Shiqi on this account, and the two became very close.

sentences.zh: 帝亦益親厚之，先後所賜珍果、牢醴、金綺衣、幣、書器無算。

translations.literal: The emperor also grew ever more intimate and generous toward him; rare fruits, feast supplies, brocade robes, silks, and books and vessels bestowed on him before and after were beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also grew ever more intimate and generous toward him; rare fruits, feast supplies, brocade robes, silks, and books and vessels bestowed on him before and after were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 宣宗崩，英宗即位，方九齡。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong died, Yingzong took the throne at just nine years of age.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong died, Yingzong acceded at the age of nine.

sentences.zh: 軍國大政關白太皇太后。

translations.literal: Great affairs of army and state were reported to the grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Major military and civil affairs were referred to the grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后推心任士奇、榮、溥三人，有事遣中使詣閣諮議，然後裁決。

translations.literal: The empress dowager entrusted her heart to Shiqi, Rong, and Pu; when there was business she dispatched palace envoys to the Grand Secretariat for consultation, and only then decided.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager placed her full trust in Shiqi, Yang Rong, and Yang Pu. On important matters she sent palace envoys to the Grand Secretariat for consultation before deciding.

sentences.zh: 三人者亦自信，侃侃行意。

translations.literal: The three men also had confidence and carried out their intent with ease and forthrightness.
translations.idiomatic: The three men in turn acted with confidence and spoke their minds freely.

sentences.zh: 士奇首請練士卒，嚴邊防，設南京參贊機務大臣，分遣文武鎮撫江西、湖廣、河南、山東，罷偵事校尉。

translations.literal: Shiqi was first to request drilling soldiers, tightening frontier defense, establishing a Nanjing coordinator of military affairs, dispatching civil and military officials to pacify Jiangxi, Huguang, Henan, and Shandong, and abolishing investigative guards.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi first urged drilling troops, strengthening frontier defenses, appointing a Nanjing coordinator of military affairs, dispatching civil and military officials to pacify Jiangxi, Huguang, Henan, and Shandong, and abolishing the secret police.

sentences.zh: 又請以次蠲租稅，慎刑獄，嚴核百司。

translations.literal: He also requested remitting rents and taxes in stages, being cautious in criminal cases, and strictly auditing the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged staged tax relief, careful handling of criminal cases, and strict auditing of government offices.

sentences.zh: 皆允行。

translations.literal: All were approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 正統之初，朝政清明，士奇等之力也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong, court government was clear and bright—this was the force of Shiqi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The clarity of government at the start of the Zhengtong reign was largely due to Shiqi and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 三年，《宣宗實錄》成，進少師。

translations.literal: In the third year the Veritable Records of Xuanzong were completed, and he was advanced to junior preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the Veritable Records of Xuanzong were completed, he was promoted to junior preceptor.

sentences.zh: 四年乞致仕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 敕歸省墓。

translations.literal: He was ordered by edict to return and visit his ancestral tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He was permitted to return home to tend his family's graves.

sentences.zh: 未幾，還。

translations.literal: Before long he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to court.

sentences.zh: 是時中官王振有寵於帝，漸預外庭事，導帝以嚴御下，大臣往往下獄。

translations.literal: At that time the eunuch Wang Zhen had the emperor's favor and gradually participated in outer-court affairs, guiding the emperor to rule subordinates strictly; ministers were often sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: By then the eunuch Wang Zhen had won the emperor's favor and gradually intruded on outer-court affairs, urging the emperor to rule his ministers harshly. Many senior officials were thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 靖江王佐敬私饋榮金。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingjiang, Zuo Jing, privately presented gold to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jingjiang, Zhu Zuojing, secretly gave Yang Rong a gift of gold.

sentences.zh: 榮先省墓，歸不之知。

translations.literal: Rong had first gone to visit his tombs and, on returning, did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong had been away visiting his family's graves and knew nothing of it when he returned.

sentences.zh: 振欲藉以傾榮，士奇力解之，得已。

translations.literal: Zhen wished to use this to overthrow Rong; Shiqi vigorously interceded, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen tried to use the incident to destroy Yang Rong, but Shiqi intervened forcefully and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 榮尋卒，士奇、溥益孤。

translations.literal: Rong soon died, and Shiqi and Pu grew yet more isolated.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong soon died, leaving Shiqi and Yang Pu increasingly isolated.

sentences.zh: 其明年遂大興師征麓川，帑藏耗費，士馬物故者數萬。

translations.literal: The next year a great army was raised to campaign against Lucchuan; the treasury was drained, and soldiers and horses lost numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The following year a major campaign was launched against Lucchuan, draining the treasury and costing tens of thousands of men and horses.

sentences.zh: 又明年，太皇太后崩，振勢益盛，大作威福，百官小有牴牾，輒執而系之。

translations.literal: The year after, the grand empress dowager died; Zhen's power grew yet greater, and he greatly wielded authority and favor—if the hundred officials had the slightest friction, he would seize and bind them.
translations.idiomatic: The year after, the grand empress dowager died. Wang Zhen's power grew unchecked. He ruled by terror, and any official who crossed him was seized and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 廷臣人人惴恐，士奇亦弗能制也。

translations.literal: Every court minister lived in fear, and Shiqi also could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials lived in fear, and even Shiqi could no longer restrain him.

sentences.zh: 士奇既耄，子稷傲很，嘗侵暴殺人。

translations.literal: Shiqi being already aged, his son Ji was arrogant and harsh and once committed aggression and killing.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi was now elderly, and his son Yang Ji was arrogant and violent, once killing a man in an act of bullying.

sentences.zh: 言官交章劾稷。

translations.literal: Censorial officials submitted memorials one after another impeaching Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Censors memorialized in succession to impeach Yang Ji.

sentences.zh: 朝議不即加法，封其狀示士奇。

translations.literal: Court discussion did not immediately apply the law; the documents were sealed and shown to Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: The court held off on immediate punishment and sealed the memorials to show Shiqi.

sentences.zh: 復有人發稷橫虐數十事，遂下之理。

translations.literal: Again someone reported several tens of Ji's acts of tyrannical cruelty, and he was thereupon sent down for trial according to law.
translations.idiomatic: More accusers came forward with dozens of charges against Yang Ji's bullying and cruelty, and he was at last arrested and brought to trial.

sentences.zh: 士奇以老疾在告。

translations.literal: Shiqi, on account of old age and illness, was on leave reporting sickness.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi was on sick leave, suffering from age and illness.

sentences.zh: 天子恐傷士奇意，降詔慰勉。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, fearing to hurt Shiqi's feelings, issued an edict to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, not wishing to distress Shiqi, issued an edict to comfort and reassure him.

sentences.zh: 士奇感泣，憂不能起。

translations.literal: Shiqi was moved to tears; grief so weighed on him that he could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi wept in gratitude and grief, and was so overcome with sorrow that he could not get out of bed.

sentences.zh: 九年三月卒，年八十。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year he died, age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of the ninth year of Zhengtong (1444), at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，諡文貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Grand Preceptor, with the posthumous name Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, with the posthumous name Wen Zhen ("Cultured and Steadfast").

sentences.zh: 有司乃論殺稷。

translations.literal: The authorities then adjudicated and executed Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The officials then condemned Yang Ji to death and executed him.

sentences.zh: 初，正統初，士奇言瓦剌漸強，將為邊患，而邊軍缺馬，恐不能御。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the beginning of Zhengtong, Shiqi said the Oirat were gradually growing strong and would become a border calamity, yet the border armies lacked horses and he feared they would be unable to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengtong reign, Shiqi had warned that the Oirat were growing stronger and would menace the borders, and that with the frontier armies short of horses they might prove unable to defend against them.

sentences.zh: 請於附近太僕寺關領，西番貢馬亦悉給之。

translations.literal: He requested to draw them from the nearby Imperial Stud offices, and that tribute horses from the Western Fan also all be given to them.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that horses be issued from nearby imperial stud farms and that all horses sent as tribute from the western tribes be allocated to the border forces.

sentences.zh: 士奇歿未幾，也先果入寇，有土木之難，識者思其言。

translations.literal: Not long after Shiqi's death, Esen indeed invaded, and there was the Tumu disaster; those who understood recalled his words.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Shiqi's death, Esen did invade, bringing the Tumu Crisis—and those who had understood his warning remembered what he had said.

sentences.zh: 又雅善知人，好推轂寒士，所薦達有初未識面者。

translations.literal: He was also by nature good at knowing men, fond of promoting humble scholars, and among those he recommended and elevated were some he had never met at the outset.
translations.idiomatic: He also had a gift for judging character and delighted in advancing obscure scholars; some men he recommended to high office he had never even met in person.

sentences.zh: 而于謙、周忱、況鍾之屬，皆用士奇薦，居官至一二十年，廉能冠天下，為世名臣雲。

translations.literal: As for such as Yu Qian, Zhou Chen, and Kuang Zhong—all advanced through Shiqi's recommendation—they held office for ten or twenty years, their probity and ability topping the realm, and became famous ministers of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian, Zhou Chen, Kuang Zhong, and others like them all rose through Shiqi's patronage; they served in high office for one or two decades, their integrity and competence unmatched in the empire, and became the era's most celebrated statesmen.

sentences.zh: 次子道，以廕補尚寶丞。

translations.literal: His second son Dao received appointment as Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat through hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: His second son, Dao, entered service as Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat by virtue of his father's rank.

sentences.zh: 成化中，進太常少卿，掌司事。

translations.literal: During the Chenghua reign he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and took charge of the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chenghua he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and served as acting head of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 楊榮，字勉仁，建安人，初名子榮。

translations.literal: Yang Rong, courtesy name Mianren, a native of Jian'an, originally named Zirong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong, styled Mianren, was a native of Jian'an; his original given name was Zirong.

sentences.zh: 建文二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the second year of Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Jianwen reign (1400).

sentences.zh: 授編修。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 成祖初入京，榮迎謁馬首曰：「殿下先謁陵乎，先即位乎？」

translations.literal: When Chengzu first entered the capital, Rong met him at his horse's head and said: "Your Highness—will you first pay respects at the tombs, or first take the throne?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor first entered Beijing, Rong greeted him at his stirrup and asked: "Your Highness—will you visit the imperial tombs first, or ascend the throne first?"

sentences.zh: 成祖遽趣駕謁陵。

translations.literal: Chengzu hurriedly spurred his carriage to pay respects at the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu at once ordered his carriage to the tombs.

sentences.zh: 自是遂受知。

translations.literal: From this he thereafter gained trust.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment he won the emperor's confidence.

sentences.zh: 既即位，簡入文淵閣，為更名榮。

translations.literal: Once enthroned, he was selected to enter the Wenyuan Pavilion and was given the new name Rong.
translations.idiomatic: After taking the throne, the emperor selected him for the Wenyuan Pavilion and renamed him Rong.

sentences.zh: 同值七人，榮最少，警敏。

translations.literal: Of the seven who served together, Rong was the youngest, alert and keen.
translations.idiomatic: Among the seven grand secretaries, Rong was the youngest—quick-witted and sharp.

sentences.zh: 一日晚，寧夏報被圍。

translations.literal: One evening, a report came that Ningxia was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: One evening came word that Ningxia was under siege.

sentences.zh: 召七人，皆已出，獨榮在，帝示以奏。

translations.literal: The seven were summoned; all had already left—only Rong remained—and the emperor showed him the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the seven secretaries, but all had gone home; only Rong was still there. The emperor showed him the report.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「寧夏城堅，人皆習戰，奏上已十余日，圍解矣。」

translations.literal: Rong said: "Ningxia's walls are strong; the men are all practiced in warfare—the memorial was submitted more than ten days ago; the siege has already been lifted."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "Ningxia's defenses are solid and its garrison is battle-hardened. That report is more than ten days old—the siege will already be over."

sentences.zh: 夜半，果奏圍解。

translations.literal: At midnight, a memorial indeed reported that the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn, a dispatch arrived confirming the siege had been raised.

sentences.zh: 帝謂榮曰：「何料之審也！」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Rong: "How accurately you foresaw it!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Rong, "Your judgment was remarkably precise!"

sentences.zh: 江西盜起，遣使撫諭，而令都督韓觀將兵繼其後。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Jiangxi; envoys were dispatched to pacify and instruct them, while Regional Commander Han Guan was ordered to lead troops in their wake.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits broke out in Jiangxi, the court sent envoys to negotiate their surrender while ordering Regional Commander Han Guan to follow with an army.

sentences.zh: 賊就撫奏至，帝欲賜敕勞觀。

translations.literal: A memorial arrived that the bandits had submitted to pacification; the emperor wished to grant an imperial letter commending Han Guan.
translations.idiomatic: When news arrived that the bandits had submitted, the emperor wanted to issue an edict praising Han Guan.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「計發奏時，觀尚未至，不得論功。」

translations.literal: Rong said: "Calculating from when the memorial was dispatched, Guan had not yet arrived—credit cannot be awarded."
translations.idiomatic: Rong objected: "When that report was sent, Han Guan had not even arrived—he cannot be given credit."

sentences.zh: 帝益重之，再遷至侍講。

translations.literal: The emperor valued him all the more and promoted him again to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought even more highly of him and promoted him again to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 太子立，進右諭德，仍兼前職，與在直諸臣同賜二品服。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was installed, he was promoted to Right Mentor and still held his previous post; together with the officials on duty he was granted second-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was installed, Rong was made Right Mentor while retaining his earlier office; he and the other officials on palace duty were granted second-rank court dress.

sentences.zh: 評議諸司事宜，稱旨，復賜衣幣。

translations.literal: In evaluating the affairs of the various offices, he pleased the emperor, and robes and silks were again bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: His review of departmental business pleased the emperor, who again rewarded him with robes and gifts of silk.

sentences.zh: 帝威嚴，與諸大臣議事未決，或至發怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was awe-inspiring; when deliberating with the great ministers matters remained unresolved, he sometimes even flew into anger.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's temper was formidable; when deliberations with his ministers reached deadlock he would sometimes explode in rage.

sentences.zh: 榮至，輒為霽顏，事亦遂決。

translations.literal: When Rong arrived, the emperor's face would clear, and the matter would then be decided.
translations.idiomatic: But when Rong appeared, the emperor's face would soften and the business would promptly reach a decision.

sentences.zh: 五年，命往甘肅經畫軍務，所過覽山川形勢，察軍民，閱城堡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was ordered to go to Gansu to organize military affairs; wherever he passed he surveyed the terrain and topography, inspected troops and civilians, and reviewed castles and forts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1407) he was dispatched to Gansu to oversee military affairs, surveying terrain along the way, inspecting troops and civilians, and reviewing fortifications.

sentences.zh: 還奏武英殿。

translations.literal: Returning, he reported in the Hall of Martial Glory.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he briefed the emperor in the Hall of Martial Glory.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，值盛暑，親剖瓜啖之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; it being the height of summer, he personally cut open a melon and fed it to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted. In the midsummer heat he personally sliced a melon and offered it to Rong.

sentences.zh: 尋進右庶子，兼職如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Right Sub-Reader and his concurrent posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Sub-Reader while keeping his other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 明年以父喪給傳歸。

translations.literal: The next year, on his father's death, he was granted post-horses and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, upon his father's death, he was granted official transport and returned home for mourning.

sentences.zh: 既葬，起復視事。

translations.literal: Once the burial was complete, he was recalled to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral he was recalled from mourning to resume office.

sentences.zh: 又明年，母喪乞歸。

translations.literal: The year after that, on his mother's death he requested to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that, when his mother died, he asked to return home for mourning.

sentences.zh: 帝以北行期迫不許，命同胡廣、金幼孜扈從。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the northern expedition's deadline was pressing, did not permit it and ordered him to accompany him together with Hu Guang and Jin Youzi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, with a northern campaign imminent, refused the request and ordered Rong to accompany him alongside Hu Guang and Jin Youzi.

sentences.zh: 甘肅總兵官何福言脫脫不花等請降，需命於亦集乃。

translations.literal: He Fu, supreme commander in Gansu, reported that Toghon Taishi and others requested surrender and awaited orders at Yijinai.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu, regional commander in Gansu, reported that Toghon Taishi and others sought to surrender and were awaiting instructions at Yijinai (Ejin).

sentences.zh: 命榮往甘肅偕福受降，持節即軍中封福寧遠侯。

translations.literal: Rong was ordered to go to Gansu together with He Fu to accept the surrender, bearing credentials to enfeoff He Fu on the spot in the army as Marquis of Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was sent to Gansu with He Fu to accept the surrender, carrying imperial credentials to ennoble He Fu as Marquis of Ningyuan there in the field.

sentences.zh: 因至寧夏，與寧陽侯陳懋規畫邊務。

translations.literal: He then went to Ningxia and together with Chen Mao, Marquis of Ningyang, planned frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He continued on to Ningxia, where with Marquis Chen Mao of Ningyang he drew up plans for frontier administration.

sentences.zh: 還陳便宜十事。

translations.literal: On returning he submitted ten proposals for timely advantage.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he submitted ten practical recommendations for border policy.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved them with commendation.

sentences.zh: 八年從出塞，次臚朐河。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed on the campaign beyond the frontier and encamped at the Lüqu River.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1410) he accompanied the emperor on campaign beyond the frontier, halting at the Lüqu River.

sentences.zh: 選勇士三百人為衛，不以隸諸將，令榮領之。

translations.literal: Three hundred brave warriors were selected as a guard corps, not placed under any general's command, and Rong was ordered to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred elite warriors were chosen as an imperial guard, placed outside the normal chain of command, with Rong put in charge.

sentences.zh: 師旋，餉不繼。

translations.literal: As the army turned back, rations did not follow in succession.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home, supplies ran out.

sentences.zh: 榮請盡以供御之余給軍，而令軍中有餘者得相貸，入塞，官為倍償。

translations.literal: Rong requested that all surplus from the imperial supplies be given to the army, and that soldiers with surplus be allowed to lend to one another; upon entering the frontier passes, the state would repay double.
translations.idiomatic: Rong proposed distributing all surplus provisions from the imperial commissary among the troops, allowing soldiers with extra rations to lend to comrades; once back inside the frontier, the government would repay them at double the amount.

sentences.zh: 軍賴以濟。

translations.literal: The army relied on this to get through.
translations.idiomatic: The army made it through on this arrangement.

sentences.zh: 明年乞奔喪，命中官護行。

translations.literal: The next year he requested urgent leave for mourning; the emperor ordered a eunuch to escort him on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he sought leave to rush home for mourning; the emperor sent a eunuch to escort him.

sentences.zh: 還詢閩中民情及歲豐歉，榮具以對。

translations.literal: On his return the emperor inquired about the people's sentiments in Minzhong and whether the harvests were ample or lean; Rong answered fully.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, the emperor asked about conditions in Fujian—the people's welfare and whether harvests had been good or poor—and Rong answered in detail.

sentences.zh: 尋命侍諸皇孫讀書文華殿。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to attend the reading of the various imperial grandsons in the Hall of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to tutor the imperial grandsons in the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 十年，甘肅守臣宋琥言，叛寇老的罕逃赤斤蒙古，且為邊患。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Gansu frontier official Song Hu reported that the rebel Lao Dehan had fled to the Chijin Mongols and would become a border menace.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1412), Song Hu, the Gansu frontier commissioner, reported that the rebel Lao Dehan had taken refuge with the Chijin Mongols and was threatening the border.

sentences.zh: 乃復遣榮至陝西，會豐城侯李彬議進兵方略。

translations.literal: Rong was again dispatched to Shaanxi to confer with Li Bin, Marquis of Fengcheng, on a strategy for advancing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was again sent to Shaanxi to confer with Marquis Li Bin of Fengcheng on a plan of campaign.

sentences.zh: 榮還奏言：「隆冬非用兵時，且有罪不過數人，兵未可出。」

translations.literal: Rong returned and memorialized: "Deep winter is not the time for deploying troops; moreover, the guilty are no more than a few men—the army should not be sent out."
