translations.idiomatic: Rong reported back: "Deep winter is no season for war, and only a handful of men are guilty—the army ought not march."

sentences.zh: 帝從其言，叛者亦降。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his words, and the rebels also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and the rebels surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 明年復與廣、幼孜從北巡。

translations.literal: The next year he again accompanied Guang and Youzi on the northern tour.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again joined Hu Guang and Jin Youzi on the northern inspection tour.

sentences.zh: 又明年征瓦剌，太孫侍行。

translations.literal: The year after that they campaigned against the Oirat, and the imperial great-grandson accompanied them.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that came the campaign against the Oirat, with the heir apparent's son accompanying the army.

sentences.zh: 帝命榮以間陳說經史，兼領尚寶事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Rong, in spare moments, to expound the classics and histories, and concurrently to oversee the Imperial Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Rong instruct the heir in the classics and history during idle hours, and also placed him in charge of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 凡宣詔出令，及旗志符驗，必得榮奏乃發。

translations.literal: Whenever proclamations and orders were issued, as well as flags, tokens, and credentials—all required Rong's memorial before they could be dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: No edicts, orders, banners, seals, or credentials could be issued without Rong's approval.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗晚坐行幄，召榮計兵食。

translations.literal: The emperor once sat late in the campaign tent and summoned Rong to deliberate on troops and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: One evening in the field the emperor summoned Rong to discuss troop supplies.

sentences.zh: 榮對曰：「擇將屯田，訓練有方，耕耨有時，即兵食足矣。」

translations.literal: Rong replied: "Choose commanders for garrison farming, train with method, plow and weed at the proper season—then troops and provisions will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Rong replied, "Select officers for frontier farming garrisons, drill the men properly, and sow and harvest on schedule—that alone will keep the army fed."

sentences.zh: 十四年與金幼孜俱進翰林學士，仍兼庶子，從還京師。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he and Jin Youzi were both promoted to Hanlin Academician, still holding the sub-reader post concurrently, and followed the emperor back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1416) he and Jin Youzi were both promoted to Hanlin Academician while retaining their posts as tutors; they returned to the capital with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 明年復從北征。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he again followed on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he again joined the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 十六年，胡廣卒，命榮掌翰林院事，益見親任。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Hu Guang died; Rong was ordered to take charge of Hanlin Academy affairs and was even more personally entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1418) Hu Guang died; Rong was put in charge of the Hanlin Academy and grew even closer to the emperor's confidence.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣多忌榮，欲疏之，共舉為祭酒。

translations.literal: Many of the great ministers were jealous of Rong and wished to distance him; together they recommended him as Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Many ministers envied Rong and schemed to sideline him, jointly recommending him for chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾固知其可，第求代榮者。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have always known he is capable—only find someone to replace Rong."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "I know full well he can do it—just find me someone to replace Rong."

sentences.zh: 諸大臣乃不敢言。

translations.literal: The great ministers then did not dare speak further.
translations.idiomatic: At that the ministers fell silent.

sentences.zh: 十八年進文淵閣大學士，兼學士如故。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, his concurrent academicianship remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1420) he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion while retaining his Hanlin posts.

sentences.zh: 明年定都北京。

translations.literal: The next year the capital was fixed at Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Beijing was established as the permanent capital.

sentences.zh: 會三殿災，榮麾衛士出圖籍制誥，舁東華門外。

translations.literal: When the three halls suffered fire, Rong commanded the guards to bring out the archives, statutes, and edicts and carry them outside the East Flowery Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When fire destroyed the three main palaces, Rong directed the guards to rescue the archives and imperial documents and carry them outside the East Flowery Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝褒之。

translations.literal: The emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 榮與幼孜陳便宜十事。

translations.literal: Rong together with Youzi submitted ten proposals of timely advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Jin Youzi submitted ten practical policy recommendations.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Approval finally came.

sentences.zh: 二十年，復從出塞，軍事悉令參決，賚予優渥。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he again followed beyond the frontier; all military matters were entirely entrusted to him for joint decision, and rewards and grants were generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1422) he again joined the campaign beyond the passes; the emperor put him in charge of all military decisions and showered him with lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 師還，勞將士，分四等賜宴，榮、幼孜皆列前席，受上賞。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the emperor feasted the officers and men, dividing them into four grades for banquets; Rong and Youzi both were placed at the front seats and received the highest rewards.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, the emperor held a feast for the troops in four tiers of honor; Rong and Jin Youzi both sat at the head table and received the highest gifts.

sentences.zh: 已，復下詔征阿魯台。

translations.literal: Soon after, an edict was again issued to campaign against Arughtai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward another edict went out for a campaign against Arughtai.

sentences.zh: 或請調建文時江西所集民兵。

translations.literal: Some proposed mobilizing the militia gathered in Jiangxi during the Jianwen reign.
translations.idiomatic: Some officials proposed re-mobilizing the militia conscripted in Jiangxi during the Jianwen reign.

sentences.zh: 帝問榮。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Rong's opinion.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「陛下許民復業且二十年，一旦復征之，非示天下信。」

translations.literal: Rong said: "Your Majesty permitted the people to return to their occupations for nearly twenty years—suddenly to conscript them again would not show the realm good faith."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "Your Majesty has allowed these people to resume farming for nearly twenty years—suddenly calling them up again would betray the trust of the empire."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 明年從出塞，軍務悉委榮，晝夜見無時。

translations.literal: The next year he followed beyond the frontier; military affairs were entirely entrusted to Rong, who was received day and night at no fixed hour.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Rong again joined the frontier campaign; the emperor delegated all military affairs to him and summoned him at all hours, day and night.

sentences.zh: 帝時稱「楊學士」，不名也。

translations.literal: The emperor at times addressed him as "Academician Yang," not calling him by name.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor habitually called him "Academician Yang" rather than by his personal name—a mark of exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 又明年復從北征。

translations.literal: The year after that he again followed on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he joined yet another northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝凡五齣塞，士卒飢凍，饋運不繼，死亡十二三。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had altogether sallied beyond the frontier five times; soldiers suffered hunger and cold, transport of supplies did not follow, and one or two in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor had led five campaigns beyond the frontier; the troops endured hunger and frost, supplies failed to keep up, and as many as two or three in ten perished.

sentences.zh: 大軍抵答蘭納木兒河，不見敵。

translations.literal: The great army reached the Dalai Namir River but found no enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The main force reached the Dalai Namir River but encountered no enemy.

sentences.zh: 帝問群臣當復進否，群臣唯唯，惟榮、幼孜從容言宜班師。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the ministers whether they should advance further; the ministers assented vaguely—only Rong and Youzi calmly said they should withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers whether to press on; the rest murmured vague assent, but only Rong and Jin Youzi calmly advised withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 還次榆木川，帝崩。

translations.literal: On the return they encamped at Yumuchuan; the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home the army halted at Yumuchuan, where the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 中官馬雲等莫知所措，密與榮、幼孜入御幄議。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Ma Yun and others did not know what to do; secretly they entered the imperial tent with Rong and Youzi to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs, led by Ma Yun, were at a loss; they withdrew with Rong and Jin Youzi into the imperial tent for a secret council.

sentences.zh: 二人議：六師在外，去京師尚遠，秘不發喪。

translations.literal: The two men deliberated: the six armies were abroad and still far from the capital—they should secretly not announce the death.
translations.idiomatic: The two men agreed: with the entire army still in the field and far from the capital, they must keep the death secret.

sentences.zh: 以禮斂，熔錫為椑，載輿中。

translations.literal: They laid out the body according to ritual, melted tin to make a coffin, and loaded it in a carriage.
translations.idiomatic: They prepared the body according to ritual, sealed it in a coffin wrought from molten tin, and loaded it onto an imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 所至朝夕進膳如常儀，益嚴軍令，人莫測。

translations.literal: Wherever they halted, morning and evening meals were served as in the usual rites; military discipline was tightened all the more—no one could fathom the truth.
translations.idiomatic: At each camp they maintained the daily ritual of presenting meals to the emperor as though nothing were amiss, tightened military discipline, and kept everyone in the dark.

sentences.zh: 或請因他事為敕，馳報皇太子。

translations.literal: Some proposed using some other matter as pretext for an edict and galloping to report to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Someone suggested sending a dispatch to the crown prince under cover of some other official business.

sentences.zh: 二人曰：「誰敢爾！

translations.literal: The two men said: "Who would dare do such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: The two men objected, "Who would dare!

sentences.zh: 先帝在則稱敕，賓天而稱敕，詐也，罪不小。」

translations.literal: When the late emperor lived one spoke of an edict—after he has ascended to Heaven yet still to speak of an edict is fraud, and the crime is no small one."
translations.idiomatic: While the late emperor lived, an edict spoke with his authority—but to issue an edict after he has died would be a fraud, and the penalty for that would be severe."

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The crowd said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: All present agreed: "Indeed."

sentences.zh: 乃具大行月日及遺命傳位意，啟太子。

translations.literal: Thereupon they fully set forth the date of the late emperor's passing and the testamentary intent to transfer the throne, and opened communication with the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: They then drew up a full account of the date of the late emperor's death and of his dying wish to pass the throne, and sent word to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 榮與少監海壽先馳訃。

translations.literal: Rong together with the Assistant Director Hai Shou first galloped ahead with the news of death.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and the assistant director Hai Shou rode ahead first to bear the tidings of the emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 既至，太子命與蹇義、楊士奇議諸所宜行者。

translations.literal: When they arrived, the crown prince ordered them to discuss with Jian Yi and Yang Shiqi all measures that ought to be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Once they arrived, the crown prince ordered them to confer with Jian Yi and Yang Shiqi on every measure that should be carried out.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，進太常卿，余官如故。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, he was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his other offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong ascended the throne, Rong was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, his other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 尋進太子少傅、謹身殿大學士。

translations.literal: Soon after he was further promoted to Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was further made Junior Tutor to the crown prince and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall.

sentences.zh: 既而有言榮當大行時，所行喪禮及處分軍事狀。

translations.literal: Before long there was word of how Rong, during the late emperor's funeral journey, had conducted mourning rites and disposed of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward word reached the court of how Rong had handled the mourning rites and military dispositions during the late emperor's funeral procession.

sentences.zh: 帝賜敕褒勞，賚予甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor granted an edict commending and rewarding him, with gifts exceedingly generous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict praising and rewarding him, with gifts of extraordinary generosity.

sentences.zh: 進工部尚書，食三祿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Works, drawing triple stipends.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Works and granted triple stipends.

sentences.zh: 時士奇、淮皆辭尚書祿，榮、幼孜亦固辭。

translations.literal: At the time Shiqi and Huang Huai both declined their ministerial stipends; Rong and Jin Youzi also firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shiqi and Huang Huai both declined their ministerial salaries, and Rong and Jin Youzi likewise refused firmly.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年，漢王高煦反。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande, the Prince of Han, Gao Xu, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 1, the Prince of Han, Zhu Gaoxu, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 帝召榮等定計。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Rong and the others to settle on a plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Rong and his colleagues to decide on a course of action.

sentences.zh: 榮首請帝親征，曰：「彼謂陛下新立，必不自行。

translations.literal: Rong was the first to ask that the emperor lead the campaign in person, saying: "They believe Your Majesty has only just ascended the throne and will surely not go yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was the first to urge the emperor to take the field in person, saying, "They assume Your Majesty has only just come to the throne and will surely not go yourself.

sentences.zh: 今出不意，以天威臨之，事無不濟。」

translations.literal: If you now move against them unexpectedly and confront them with Heaven's majesty, nothing will fail to succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Strike now when they do not expect it, and confront them with the majesty of Heaven—nothing will fail to succeed."

sentences.zh: 帝從其計。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted his plan.

sentences.zh: 至樂安，高煦出降。

translations.literal: When they reached Le'an, Gaoxu came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Le'an, Gaoxu came out and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 師還，以決策功，受上賞，賜銀章五，褒予甚至。

translations.literal: When the army returned, for his merit in the decision he received the highest reward; five silver seals were bestowed, and commendation and gifts were lavished to an extraordinary degree.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he received the highest reward for his counsel in the decision: five silver seals were bestowed, and praise and gifts were heaped upon him to a remarkable degree.

sentences.zh: 三年從帝巡邊，至遵化。

translations.literal: In the third year he accompanied the emperor on a border tour as far as Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he accompanied the emperor on a tour of the frontier as far as Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 聞兀良哈將寇邊，帝留扈行諸文臣於大營，獨命榮從。

translations.literal: Hearing that the Uriankhai were about to raid the frontier, the emperor left all the civil officials who had accompanied him at the great camp and ordered Rong alone to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the Uriankhai were about to raid the border, the emperor left the civil officials who had accompanied him at the main camp and ordered Rong alone to follow.

sentences.zh: 自將輕騎出喜峰口，破敵而還。

translations.literal: He personally led light cavalry out through Xifeng Pass, routed the enemy, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself led light cavalry out through Xifeng Pass, defeated the enemy, and returned.

sentences.zh: 五年進少傅，辭大學士祿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Junior Tutor and declined the Grand Secretary stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to Junior Tutor and declined the salary attached to his Grand Secretary post.

sentences.zh: 九年復從巡邊，至洗馬林而還。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again accompanied the border tour, reaching Ximolin before returning.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he again accompanied the frontier tour, going as far as Ximolin before turning back.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，委寄如故。

translations.literal: When Yingzong took the throne, the trust placed in him was as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong ascended the throne, the confidence reposed in him remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 正統三年，與士奇俱進少師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong, he and Shiqi were both promoted to Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengtong, he and Shiqi were both promoted to Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 五年乞歸展墓，命中官護行。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he requested leave to return and visit his ancestral tombs; the emperor ordered eunuchs to escort him on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he asked to return home to tend his ancestral graves, and the emperor ordered eunuchs to escort him on the journey.

sentences.zh: 還至武林驛而卒，年七十。

translations.literal: On the return he died at Wulin Post Station, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: On the way back he died at Wulin Post Station, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，諡文敏，授世襲都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor, given the posthumous name Wenmin, and awarded a hereditary command as Duhu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Grand Preceptor, given the posthumous name Wenmin, and his family was granted a hereditary post as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 榮歷事四朝，謀而能斷。

translations.literal: Rong served through four reigns, deliberate in counsel and resolute in decision.
translations.idiomatic: Rong served four reigns, thoughtful in counsel and firm in decision.

sentences.zh: 永樂末，浙、閩山賊起，議發兵。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongle, mountain bandits rose in Zhejiang and Fujian, and the court debated sending troops.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yongle reign, mountain bandits rose in Zhejiang and Fujian, and the court debated dispatching troops.

sentences.zh: 帝時在塞外，奏至，以示榮。

translations.literal: The emperor was then beyond the frontier; when the memorial arrived, he showed it to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then on campaign beyond the frontier; when the memorial arrived, he showed it to Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「愚民苦有司，不得已相聚自保。

translations.literal: Rong said: "These foolish commoners suffer under local officials and have no choice but to gather together in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "These simple folk suffer under local officials and have been driven to gather together in self-defense.

sentences.zh: 兵出，將益聚不可解。

translations.literal: If troops go out, they will only gather the more and the knot will become impossible to untie.
translations.idiomatic: Send troops, and the rebels will only gather in greater numbers until the trouble cannot be undone.

sentences.zh: 遣使招撫，當不煩兵。」

translations.literal: Send envoys to summon and soothe them, and there should be no need to trouble the army."
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to summon and reassure them, and there should be no need to resort to force."

sentences.zh: 從之，盜果息。

translations.literal: [The emperor] followed this advice, and the bandits indeed subsided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice, and the bandits indeed quieted down.

sentences.zh: 安南之棄，諸大臣多謂不可，獨榮與士奇力言不宜以荒服疲中國。

translations.literal: Regarding the abandonment of Annam, most ministers said it could not be done; only Rong and Shiqi argued forcefully that China ought not exhaust itself over a distant barbarian territory.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated abandoning Annam, most ministers held that it could not be done; only Rong and Shiqi argued forcefully that the empire ought not wear itself out over a distant frontier land.

sentences.zh: 其老成持重類如此。

translations.literal: His seasoned steadiness was of this kind throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the seasoned steadiness he showed throughout.

sentences.zh: 論事激發，不能容人過。

translations.literal: In debating affairs he could be heated and would not tolerate others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: In debate he could be sharp and would not overlook others' faults.

sentences.zh: 然遇人觸帝怒致不測，往往以微言導帝意，輒得解。

translations.literal: Yet when someone aroused the emperor's wrath to the point of unpredictable punishment, he would often guide the emperor's intent with subtle words, and release would usually follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when someone had provoked the emperor's wrath to the brink of unpredictable punishment, he would often steer the emperor's mind with a few subtle words, and clemency would usually follow.

sentences.zh: 夏原吉、李時勉之不死，都御史劉觀之免戍邊，皆賴其力。

translations.literal: That Xia Yuanji and Li Shimian did not die, and that Censor-in-Chief Liu Guan was spared frontier exile—all owed to his intercession.
translations.idiomatic: That Xia Yuanji and Li Shimian were not put to death, and that Censor-in-Chief Liu Guan was spared exile to the frontier—all owed to his intervention.

sentences.zh: 嘗語人曰：「事君有體，進諫有方，以悻直取禍，吾不為也。」

translations.literal: He once told others: "Serving one's ruler has its proper form, and remonstrance has its proper method. To invite calamity through defiant bluntness—that I will not do."
translations.idiomatic: He once told others, "Serving one's ruler has its proper form, and remonstrance has its proper method. To invite disaster through reckless bluntness—that I will not do."

sentences.zh: 故其恩遇亦始終無間。

translations.literal: Therefore favor toward him remained unbroken from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason imperial favor toward him never wavered from first to last.

sentences.zh: 重修《太祖實錄》及太宗、仁、宣三朝《實錄》，皆為總裁官。

translations.literal: In the revision of the Veritable Records of Taizu and of the three reigns Taizong, Ren, and Xuan, he served as chief compiler in every case.
translations.idiomatic: In the revision of the Veritable Records of Taizu and of the Taizong, Renzong, and Xuanzong reigns, he served as chief compiler in every case.

sentences.zh: 先後賜賚，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Rewards bestowed on him over the years were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial gifts bestowed on him over the years were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 性喜賓客，雖貴盛無稍崖岸，士多歸心焉。

translations.literal: By nature he delighted in hosting guests; though exalted in rank and power, he showed not the slightest aloofness, and many men of letters gave him their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved to receive guests; though he stood at the height of rank and power, he showed not the slightest hauteur, and many scholars gave him their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 或謂榮處國家大事，不愧唐姚崇，而不拘小節，亦頗類之。

translations.literal: Some said that in handling great affairs of state Rong was not unworthy of the Tang minister Yao Chong, and that in not being bound by petty proprieties he rather resembled him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Some said that in handling great affairs of state Rong was not unworthy of comparison with the Tang minister Yao Chong, and that in his disregard for petty proprieties he rather resembled him too.

sentences.zh: 家富，曾孫曄為建寧指揮，以貲敗。

translations.literal: The family was wealthy; his great-great-grandson Ye, commandant of Jianning, was ruined through wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The family was wealthy; his great-great-grandson Ye, commandant of Jianning, was brought down through corruption of wealth.

sentences.zh: 詳《宦官傳》。

translations.literal: See the "Biographies of Eunuchs."
translations.idiomatic: For details, see the "Biographies of Eunuchs."

sentences.zh: 曾孫 旦

translations.literal: Great-great-grandson: Dan
translations.idiomatic: Great-great-grandson: Dan

sentences.zh: 曄從弟旦，字晉叔，弘治中進士。

translations.literal: Ye's younger cousin Dan, courtesy name Jingshu, was a jinshi in the Hongzhi era.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's younger cousin Dan, courtesy name Jingshu, passed the jinshi examination in the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 歷官太常卿。

translations.literal: He rose through the ranks to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 以忤劉瑾，左遷知溫州府，治最，稍遷浙江提學副使。

translations.literal: For offending Liu Jin he was demoted to prefect of Wenzhou; his governance ranked supreme, and he was gradually promoted to Vice Commissioner of Education in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: For offending Liu Jin he was demoted to prefect of Wenzhou; his administration ranked highest, and he was gradually promoted to Vice Commissioner of Education in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，累擢至戶部侍郎，督京、通倉，出理餉甘肅。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, he was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Revenue, supervising the granaries of Jing and Tong, then sent out to manage provisions in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, he was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Revenue, put in charge of the Jing and Tong granaries, and then sent out to manage supplies in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 還，進右都御史，總督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: On his return he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief and put in overall charge of military affairs in the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief and placed in overall command of military affairs in the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 討平番禺、清遠、河源諸瑤。

translations.literal: He suppressed and pacified the Yao of Panyu, Qingyuan, Heyuan, and other districts.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed and pacified the Yao of Panyu, Qingyuan, Heyuan, and other regions.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，遷至南京吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he was transferred to Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he was transferred to Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼驟進，旦率九卿極言不可。

translations.literal: When Zhang Cong and Gui E rose suddenly in rank, Dan led the Nine Ministers in declaring forcefully that this could not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong and Gui E were suddenly elevated in rank, Dan led the Nine Ministers in declaring forcefully that this must not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 會吏部尚書喬宇罷，召旦代之，未至，為給事中陳洸所劾，勒致仕。

translations.literal: When Minister of Personnel Qiao Yu was dismissed, Dan was summoned to replace him; before he arrived he was impeached by the supervising secretary Chen Guang and compelled to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Personnel Qiao Yu was dismissed, Dan was summoned to replace him; before he could take up the post he was impeached by the supervising secretary Chen Guang and forced to retire.

sentences.zh: 年七十余卒。

translations.literal: He died in his seventies.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 楊溥，字弘濟，石首人。

translations.literal: Yang Pu, courtesy name Hongji, was a native of Shishou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pu, courtesy name Hongji, was a native of Shishou.

sentences.zh: 與楊榮同舉進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Yang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Yang Rong.

sentences.zh: 授編修。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，侍皇太子為洗馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he attended the crown prince as Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongle reign he served the crown prince as Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 太子嘗讀《漢書》，稱張釋之賢。

translations.literal: The crown prince once read the Book of Han and praised Zhang Shizhi as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince once read the Book of Han and praised Zhang Shizhi as a man of worth.

sentences.zh: 溥曰：「釋之誠賢，非文帝寬仁，未得行其志也。」

translations.literal: Pu said: "Shizhi was indeed worthy, but without Emperor Wen's leniency and benevolence he could not have carried out his aims."
translations.idiomatic: Pu said, "Shizhi was indeed worthy, but without Emperor Wen's leniency and benevolence he could never have carried out his aims."

sentences.zh: 採文帝事編類以獻。

translations.literal: He gathered and classified anecdotes of Emperor Wen and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He collected and arranged anecdotes of Emperor Wen and presented them to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子大悅。

translations.literal: The crown prince was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 久之，以喪歸。

translations.literal: After a long while he returned home on mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 時太子監國，命起視事。

translations.literal: At the time the crown prince was regent; he was ordered to resume office despite mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the crown prince was regent, and Pu was ordered to leave mourning and resume office.

sentences.zh: 十二年，東宮遣使迎帝遲，帝怒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Eastern Palace sent envoys to welcome the emperor too late, and the emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the Eastern Palace sent envoys to welcome the emperor too late, and the emperor was enraged.

sentences.zh: 黃淮逮至北京繫獄。

translations.literal: Huang Huai was seized, brought to Beijing, and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Huai was seized, brought to Beijing, and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 及金問至，帝益怒曰：「問何人，得侍太子！」

translations.literal: When Jin Wen arrived as well, the emperor grew still angrier and said: "What sort of man is Wen, that he may attend the crown prince!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Wen arrived as well, the emperor grew still angrier and said, "What sort of man is Wen, that he should be allowed to attend the crown prince!"

sentences.zh: 下法司鞫，連溥，逮系錦衣衛獄。

translations.literal: [The case] was handed to the judicial offices for interrogation; Pu was implicated, seized, and confined in the prison of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The case was handed to the judicial offices for interrogation; Pu was implicated, seized, and imprisoned in the Embroidered Uniform Guard jail.

sentences.zh: 家人供食數絕。

translations.literal: Several times his family's provisions of food were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Several times his family's food supplies were cut off.

sentences.zh: 而帝意不可測，旦夕且死。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor's intent was unpredictable, and death might come at any moment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor's intent was unpredictable, and death might come at any hour.

sentences.zh: 溥益奮，讀書不輟。

translations.literal: Pu only redoubled his resolve and never stopped reading.
translations.idiomatic: Pu only redoubled his resolve and never ceased his reading.

sentences.zh: 系十年，讀經史諸子數周。

translations.literal: Imprisoned for ten years, he read through the classics, histories, and masters several times over.
translations.idiomatic: Imprisoned for ten years, he read through the classics, histories, and masters several times over.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，釋出獄，擢翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, Pu was released from prison and promoted to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne, Pu was released from prison and promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 嘗密疏言事。

translations.literal: He once submitted a sealed memorial on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted a sealed memorial on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝褒答之，賜鈔幣。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and answered him, bestowing paper money and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and answered him, bestowing paper money and silks.

sentences.zh: 已，念溥由己故久困，尤憐之。

translations.literal: Then, remembering that Pu had long suffered on his account, the emperor pitied him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Then, remembering that Pu had long suffered on his account, the emperor pitied him all the more.

sentences.zh: 明年建弘文閣於思善門左，選諸臣有學行者侍值。

translations.literal: The next year the Hongwen Pavilion was built to the left of the Sishan Gate, and learned ministers were selected to attend on duty.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Hongwen Pavilion was built to the left of the Sishan Gate, and learned ministers were selected to attend on duty.

sentences.zh: 士奇薦侍講王進、儒士陳繼，蹇義薦學錄楊敬、訓導何澄。

translations.literal: Shiqi recommended Lecturer Wang Jin and scholar Chen Ji; Jian Yi recommended school recorder Yang Jing and instructor He Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi recommended Lecturer Wang Jin and scholar Chen Ji; Jian Yi recommended school recorder Yang Jing and instructor He Cheng.

sentences.zh: 詔官繼博士，敬編修，澄給事中，日值閣中。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Ji Doctor, Jing Compiler, and Cheng Adviser-in-Attendance, with daily duty in the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Ji Doctor, Jing Compiler, and Cheng Adviser-in-Attendance, with daily duty in the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 命溥掌閣事，親授閣印，曰：「朕用卿左右，非止學問。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Pu to manage pavilion affairs, personally handing him the pavilion seal, and said: "I employ you at my side not only for learning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Pu to manage pavilion affairs, personally handing him the pavilion seal, and said, "I employ you at my side not only for learning.

sentences.zh: 欲廣知民事，為治道輔。

translations.literal: I wish to broaden my knowledge of the people's affairs and have you assist in the path of governance.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to broaden my knowledge of the people's affairs and have you assist in the path of governance.

sentences.zh: 有所建白，封識以進。」

translations.literal: Whatever you propose, seal it and submit it."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever you propose, seal it and submit it."

sentences.zh: 尋進太常卿，兼職如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while retaining his other post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while retaining his other post.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，弘文閣罷，召溥入內閣，與楊士奇等共典機務。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, the Hongwen Pavilion was abolished; Pu was summoned into the Grand Secretariat to manage state affairs together with Yang Shiqi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, the Hongwen Pavilion was abolished; Pu was summoned into the Grand Secretariat to manage state affairs together with Yang Shiqi and the others.

sentences.zh: 居四年，以母喪去，起復。

translations.literal: After four years he left office on account of his mother's death, then was recalled from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he left office upon his mother's death, then was recalled from mourning to resume duty.

sentences.zh: 九年遷禮部尚書，學士值內閣如故。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Minister of Rites, continuing to serve in the Grand Secretariat as a Grand Secretary as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to Minister of Rites while continuing to serve in the Grand Secretariat as before.

sentences.zh: 英宗初立，與士奇、榮請開經筵。

translations.literal: When Yingzong was first installed, he joined Shiqi and Rong in requesting that the classics lecture be opened.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was first enthroned, he joined Shiqi and Rong in requesting that the classics lecture be instituted.

sentences.zh: 豫擇講官，必得學識平正、言行端謹、老成達大體者數人供職。

translations.literal: They preselected lecturers, insisting on several men of solid learning and upright judgment, decorous in word and deed, seasoned and versed in the larger principles of state.
translations.idiomatic: They preselected lecturers, insisting on several men of solid learning and upright judgment, decorous in word and deed, seasoned and versed in the larger principles of state.

sentences.zh: 且請慎選宮中朝夕侍從內臣。

translations.literal: They also asked that the inner eunuchs who attended the emperor morning and evening in the palace be chosen with care.
translations.idiomatic: They also asked that the inner eunuchs who attended the emperor day and night in the palace be chosen with care.

sentences.zh: 太后大喜。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 一日，太后坐便殿，帝西向立，召英國公張輔及士奇、榮、溥、尚書胡濙入。

translations.literal: One day the empress dowager sat in an informal hall; the emperor stood facing west and summoned the Duke of Yingguo Zhang Fu, together with Shiqi, Rong, Pu, and Minister Hu Ying.
translations.idiomatic: One day the empress dowager sat in an informal hall; the emperor stood facing west and summoned the Duke of Yingguo Zhang Fu, together with Shiqi, Rong, Pu, and Minister Hu Ying.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「卿等老臣，嗣君幼，幸同心共安社稷。」

translations.literal: She instructed them: "You are aged ministers; the heir is young. I trust you will join hearts and together secure the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: She addressed them: "You are aged ministers; the new ruler is young. I trust you will join in one heart to secure the altars of state together."

sentences.zh: 又召溥前曰：「仁宗皇帝念卿忠，屢加嘆息，不意今尚見卿。」

translations.literal: She then called Pu forward and said: "Emperor Renzong often thought of your loyalty and sighed over it again and again; I never expected to see you still here today."
translations.idiomatic: She then called Pu forward and said, "Emperor Renzong often thought of your loyalty and sighed over it again and again; I never expected to see you still here today."

sentences.zh: 溥感泣，太后亦泣，左右皆悲愴。

translations.literal: Pu wept in gratitude; the empress dowager wept as well, and all those beside them were overcome with sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Pu wept in gratitude; the empress dowager wept as well, and all those present were overcome with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 始仁宗為太子，被讒，宮僚多死詔獄，溥及黃淮一系十年，瀕死者數矣。

translations.literal: At the outset, when Renzong was crown prince, he was slandered; many of his palace staff died in the imperial prison. Pu and Huang Huai were each imprisoned for ten years and several times came near death.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, when Renzong was crown prince, he was slandered; many of his palace staff died in the imperial prison. Pu and Huang Huai were each imprisoned for ten years and several times came near death.

sentences.zh: 仁宗時時於宮中念諸臣，太后亦久憐之，故為溥言之如此。

translations.literal: Renzong had often remembered these ministers within the palace, and the empress dowager had long pitied them—hence she spoke to Pu in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong had often remembered these ministers within the palace, and the empress dowager had long pitied them—hence she spoke to Pu in this way.

sentences.zh: 太后復顧帝曰：「此五臣，三朝簡任，俾輔後人。

translations.literal: The empress dowager again turned to the emperor and said: "These five ministers were chosen through three reigns to assist those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager again turned to the emperor and said, "These five ministers were chosen across three reigns to assist those who come after.

sentences.zh: 皇帝萬幾，宜與五臣共計。」

translations.literal: In the myriad affairs of state, Your Majesty should consult with these five ministers."
translations.idiomatic: In the myriad affairs of state, Your Majesty should consult with these five ministers."

sentences.zh: 正統三年，《宣宗實錄》成，進少保、武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong, when the Veritable Records of Xuanzong were completed, he was promoted to Junior Guardian and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengtong, when the Veritable Records of Xuanzong were completed, he was promoted to Junior Guardian and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 溥後士奇、榮二十餘年入閣，至是乃與士奇、榮並。

translations.literal: Pu had entered the Grand Secretariat more than twenty years after Shiqi and Rong; only now was he placed on equal footing with them.
translations.idiomatic: Pu had entered the Grand Secretariat more than twenty years after Shiqi and Rong; only now was he placed on equal footing with them.

sentences.zh: 六年歸省墓，尋還。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he returned home to tend his ancestral graves, and soon came back.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he returned home to tend his ancestral graves, and soon came back.

sentences.zh: 是時，王振尚未橫，天下清平，朝無失政，中外臣民翕然稱「三楊」。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Zhen had not yet grown overbearing; the realm was tranquil, the court committed no misgovernment, and officials and people within and without all spoke as one of the "Three Yangs."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Zhen had not yet grown overbearing; the realm was at peace, the court committed no misgovernment, and officials and people everywhere spoke as one of the "Three Yangs."

sentences.zh: 以居第目士奇曰「西楊」，榮曰「東楊」，而溥嘗自署郡望曰南郡，因號為「南楊」。

translations.literal: By their residences Shiqi was called "Western Yang," Rong "Eastern Yang," and as Pu sometimes styled himself by his ancestral district as Nanjun, he came to be known as "Southern Yang."
translations.idiomatic: By their residences Shiqi was called "Western Yang," Rong "Eastern Yang," and as Pu sometimes styled himself by his ancestral district as Nanjun, he came to be known as "Southern Yang."

sentences.zh: 溥質直廉靜，無城府。

translations.literal: Pu was plain, upright, frugal, and quiet, without hidden designs.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was plain, upright, frugal, and quiet, without hidden designs.

sentences.zh: 性恭謹，每入朝，循牆而走。

translations.literal: By nature deferential and careful, whenever he entered court he walked along the wall.
translations.idiomatic: By nature deferential and careful, whenever he entered court he walked along the wall.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣論事爭可否，或至違言。

translations.literal: When the other ministers debated affairs and disputed points pro and con, disagreements sometimes even reached open contradiction.
translations.idiomatic: When the other ministers debated affairs and disputed points pro and con, disagreements sometimes even broke into open contradiction.

sentences.zh: 溥平心處之，諸大臣皆嘆服。

translations.literal: Pu handled matters with an even mind, and all the great ministers sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Pu met them with equanimity, and the senior ministers all admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 時謂士奇有學行，榮有才識，溥有雅操，皆人所不及雲。

translations.literal: At the time it was said that Shiqi had learning and conduct, Rong had talent and judgment, and Pu had refined integrity—each beyond what others could match.
translations.idiomatic: People said Shiqi had learning and moral stature, Rong talent and insight, and Pu refined integrity—qualities none could match.

sentences.zh: 比榮、士奇相繼卒，在閣者馬愉、高谷、曹鼐皆後進望輕。

translations.literal: When Rong and Shiqi died in succession, those in the Grand Secretariat—Ma Yu, Gao Gu, and Cao Tai—were all juniors of slight standing.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong and Shiqi died in turn, the men left in the Grand Secretariat—Ma Yu, Gao Gu, and Cao Tai—were junior officials of little weight.

sentences.zh: 溥孤立，王振益用事。

translations.literal: Pu stood alone, and Wang Zhen wielded power ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was isolated, and Wang Zhen's influence grew unchecked.

sentences.zh: 十一年七月，溥卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eleventh year Pu died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eleventh year he died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，諡文定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the temple name Wendi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Wendi.

sentences.zh: 官其孫壽尚寶司丞。

translations.literal: His grandson Shou was given office as assistant director of the Imperial Seals Office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shou was appointed assistant director of the Imperial Seals Office.

sentences.zh: 後三年，振遂導英宗北征，陷土木，幾至大亂。

translations.literal: Three years later Zhen led Yingzong on the northern campaign, and at Tumu disaster nearly brought the realm to chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Wang Zhen led Yingzong north, and the disaster at Tumu nearly plunged the empire into chaos.

sentences.zh: 時人追思此三人者在，當不至此。

translations.literal: People of the time reflected that had these three men still been alive, it would not have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations reflected that if the three men had still been alive, matters would never have reached that pass.

sentences.zh: 而後起者爭暴其短，以為依違中旨，釀成賊奄之禍，亦過刻之端也。

translations.literal: Yet those who came after vied to expose their faults, holding that by wavering to suit the imperial will they brewed the disaster of the villainous eunuch—this too was an excess of severity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet later critics competed to expose their faults, blaming their habit of trimming to the emperor's mood for the eunuch disaster—a judgment that was itself excessively harsh.

sentences.zh: 馬愉，字性和，臨朐人。

translations.literal: Ma Yu, courtesy name Xinghe, was a native of Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yu, courtesy name Xinghe, came from Linqu.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年進士第一。

translations.literal: He ranked first in the jinshi examination in the second year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked first in the jinshi examination in Xuande 2 (1427).

sentences.zh: 授翰林修撰。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，特簡史官及庶吉士三十七人進學文淵閣，以愉為首。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year, thirty-seven historians and junior compilers were specially selected to study at the Wenyuan Pavilion, with Yu at their head.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the ninth year, thirty-seven historians and junior compilers were specially selected for study at the Wenyuan Pavilion, with Yu placed first.

sentences.zh: 正統元年充經筵講官，再遷至侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong he served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium and was promoted again to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1 (1436) he served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium and was promoted again to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 時王振用事，一日，語楊士奇、榮曰：「朝廷事久勞公等，公等皆高年，倦矣。」

translations.literal: At that time Wang Zhen was in power. One day he said to Yang Shiqi and Rong: "State affairs have long burdened you gentlemen; you are all advanced in years and must be weary."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Zhen was in power. One day he said to Yang Shiqi and Rong, "State affairs have long burdened you gentlemen; you are all advanced in years and must be weary."

sentences.zh: 士奇曰：「老臣盡瘁報國，死而後已。」

translations.literal: Shiqi said: "We old ministers exhaust ourselves in service to the state and will not cease until death."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said, "We old ministers exhaust ourselves in service to the state and will not cease until death."

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「吾輩衰殘，無以效力，當擇後生可任者，報聖恩耳。」

translations.literal: Rong said: "We are worn and feeble and can no longer be of use. We ought to select younger men fit for office and repay the emperor's grace."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "We are worn and feeble and can no longer be of use. We ought to select younger men fit for office and repay the emperor's grace."

sentences.zh: 振喜而退。

translations.literal: Zhen was pleased and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was pleased and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 士奇咎榮失言。

translations.literal: Shiqi blamed Rong for speaking out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi blamed Rong for speaking out of turn.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「彼厭吾輩矣，一旦內中出片紙令某人入閣，且奈何？

translations.literal: Rong said: "He is already weary of us. If one day a slip of paper issues from the inner palace appointing someone to the Grand Secretariat, what then can we do?
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "He is already weary of us. If one day a slip of paper issues from the inner palace appointing someone to the Grand Secretariat, what then can we do?

sentences.zh: 及此時進一二賢者，同心協力，尚可為也。」

translations.literal: If we now advance one or two worthy men while we still can, joining hearts in common effort, something can still be done."
translations.idiomatic: If we now advance one or two worthy men while we still can, joining hearts in common effort, something can still be done."

sentences.zh: 士奇以為然。

translations.literal: Shiqi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi agreed.

sentences.zh: 翼日，遂列侍讀學士苗衷、侍講曹鼐及愉名以進。

translations.literal: The next day he submitted the names of Reader-in-Waiting Miao Zhong, Lecturer Cao Tai, and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he submitted the names of Reader-in-Waiting Miao Zhong, Lecturer Cao Tai, and Yu.

sentences.zh: 由是愉被擢用。

translations.literal: From this Yu was selected for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: From this Yu was selected for advancement.

sentences.zh: 五年詔以本官入內閣，參預機務，尋進禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict appointed him to the Grand Secretariat at his existing rank to deliberate on state affairs; soon after he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an edict appointed him to the Grand Secretariat at his existing rank to deliberate on state affairs; soon after he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the twelfth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書兼學士。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of minister and concurrent academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of minister with concurrent academician rank.

sentences.zh: 贈官兼職，自愉始。

translations.literal: The practice of posthumously granting offices with concurrent titles began with Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of posthumously granting offices with concurrent titles began with Yu.

sentences.zh: 愉端重簡默，門無私謁。

translations.literal: Yu was dignified, restrained, and taciturn; no private callers came to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yu was dignified, reserved, and sparing of speech, and admitted no private callers at his gate.

sentences.zh: 論事務寬厚。

translations.literal: In discussing affairs he was always generous and lenient.
translations.idiomatic: In council he always favored generous and lenient measures.

sentences.zh: 嘗奏天下獄久者多瘐死，宜簡使者分道決遣。

translations.literal: He once memorialized that in prisons throughout the realm many long detained died of illness and neglect, and that envoys should be selected to decide and release cases by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized that prisoners held too long were dying of neglect in jails across the empire, and urged dispatching commissioners on separate routes to review and settle cases.

sentences.zh: 帝納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 邊警，方命將，而別部使至，眾議執之。

translations.literal: When frontier alarms arose, generals were being appointed, and envoys from another tribe arrived; the assembly debated seizing them.
translations.idiomatic: During a frontier alert, as generals were being appointed, envoys from another branch arrived, and many at court urged seizing them.

sentences.zh: 愉言：「賞善罰惡，為治之本。

translations.literal: Yu said, "Rewarding good and punishing evil is the root of government.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Rewarding the good and punishing the wicked is the foundation of government.

sentences.zh: 波及於善，非法。

translations.literal: To extend punishment to the innocent is not according to law.
translations.idiomatic: To harm the innocent in the process is unlawful.

sentences.zh: 乘人之來執之，不武。」

translations.literal: To seize men who come in good faith is not martial honor."
translations.idiomatic: To seize envoys who come in good faith is unworthy of a great power."

sentences.zh: 帝然之，厚遣其使。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and sent the envoys away with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent the envoys away with rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：成祖時，士奇、榮與解縉等同直內閣，溥亦同為仁宗宮僚，而三人逮事四朝，為時耆碩。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: In Chengzu's time Shiqi and Rong served in the Grand Secretariat together with Xie Jin and others; Pu likewise was a palace official of Renzong—and the three men in succession served four reigns, becoming the senior worthies of their age.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Under Chengzu, Shiqi and Rong served in the Grand Secretariat with Xie Jin and others; Pu had been a palace tutor to Renzong. All three served four reigns and became the elder statesmen of their age.

sentences.zh: 溥入閣雖後，德望相亞，是以明稱賢相，必首三楊。

translations.literal: Though Pu entered the Grand Secretariat later, his virtue and standing were nearly equal; hence when the Ming speak of worthy chancellors, they always name the Three Yang first.
translations.idiomatic: Though Pu entered the cabinet last, his stature was nearly equal to the others; when the Ming speak of great ministers, they always name the Three Yang first.

sentences.zh: 均能原本儒術，通達事幾，協力相資，靖共匪懈。

translations.literal: All were able to ground themselves in Confucian learning, penetrate the turns of affairs, assist one another in concert, and labor in harmony without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: All rooted their governance in Confucian learning, understood the turns of affairs, supported one another, and served in loyal harmony without slackening.

sentences.zh: 史稱房、杜持眾美效之君，輔贊彌縫而藏諸用。

translations.literal: Histories say of Fang and Du that they held the many excellences and offered them to their lord, assisting, praising, smoothing, and concealing their use.
translations.idiomatic: Historians said of Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui that they gathered every excellence and offered it to their ruler, supporting and smoothing affairs while keeping their own contributions hidden.

sentences.zh: 又稱姚崇善應變，以成天下之務；

translations.literal: They also praise Yao Chong for skill in adapting to change and accomplishing the tasks of the realm;
translations.idiomatic: They also praised Yao Chong for adapting to change and accomplishing the empire's business;

sentences.zh: 宋璟善守文，以持天下之正。

translations.literal: and Song Jing for skill in preserving the written order and upholding the rectitude of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: and Song Jing for preserving established institutions and upholding the empire's moral order.

sentences.zh: 三楊其庶幾乎。

translations.literal: The Three Yang may be said to have nearly approached this.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Yang may be said to have come close to matching them.
